spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m2p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Gangs, Opening, MaxStake

Pool == Cardinality(Gangs) * Opening

VARIABLES balance, escrow, spent, vote, decision, active

Vars == <<balance, escrow, spent, vote, decision, active>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

\* A gang sitting on an unapplied yes vote is still holding escrowed credits,
\* and the reset zeroes escrows outright.
Unapplied == \E g \in Gangs : vote[g] = "yes"

TypeOK ==
    /\ balance \in [Gangs -> 0..(2 * Pool)] /\ spent \in 0..Pool
    /\ escrow \in [Gangs -> 0..MaxStake]
    /\ vote \in [Gangs -> {"none", "yes", "no", "applied"}]
    /\ decision \in {"none", "commit", "abort"}
    /\ active \subseteq Gangs

Init ==
    /\ balance = [g \in Gangs |-> Opening] /\ spent = 0
    /\ escrow = [g \in Gangs |-> 0]
    /\ vote = [g \in Gangs |-> "none"]
    /\ decision = "none" /\ active = Gangs

CommitStake(g, n) ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ g \in active /\ vote[g] = "none"
    /\ n <= balance[g]
    /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![g] = @ - n]
    /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![g] = n]
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![g] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spent, decision, active>>

VoteNo(g) ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ g \in active /\ vote[g] = "none"
    /\ balance[g] = 0
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![g] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, escrow, spent, decision, active>>

Decide ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ active # {}
    /\ \A g \in active : vote[g] \in {"yes", "no"}
    /\ decision' = IF \A g \in active : vote[g] = "yes" THEN "commit"
                   ELSE "abort"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, escrow, spent, vote, active>>

ApplyCommit(g) ==
    /\ decision = "commit" /\ vote[g] = "yes"
    /\ spent' = spent + escrow[g]
    /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![g] = 0]
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![g] = "applied"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, decision, active>>

ApplyAbort(g) ==
    /\ decision = "abort" /\ vote[g] = "yes"
    /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![g] = @ + escrow[g]]
    /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![g] = 0]
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![g] = "applied"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spent, decision, active>>

\* The reset zeroes every escrow, so it may only run once nobody is left
\* holding escrowed credits.
Reset ==
    /\ decision # "none" /\ ~Unapplied
    /\ decision' = "none" /\ vote' = [g \in Gangs |-> "none"]
    /\ escrow' = [g \in Gangs |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, spent, active>>

\* Capacity changes under the negotiation, but never under a vote.
Republish(as) ==
    /\ decision = "none" /\ as # {}
    /\ \A g \in Gangs \ as : vote[g] = "none"
    /\ active' = as
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, escrow, spent, vote, decision>>

VoteStep == \E g \in Gangs, n \in 1..MaxStake : CommitStake(g, n) \/ VoteNo(g)

ApplyStep == \E g \in Gangs : ApplyCommit(g) \/ ApplyAbort(g)

Next ==
    \/ VoteStep \/ Decide \/ ApplyStep \/ Reset
    \/ \E as \in SUBSET Gangs : Republish(as)

\* The active set can be republished indefinitely, so deciding and applying
\* need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(VoteStep) /\ WF_Vars(Reset)
    /\ SF_Vars(Decide) /\ SF_Vars(ApplyStep)

\* Conservation: balances plus escrows plus spent is always exactly the pool.
CreditsConserved ==
    Tally(balance, Gangs) + Tally(escrow, Gangs) + spent = Pool

\* Progress: a joint lift really does get funded.
CreditsEventuallySpent == <>(spent > 0)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Gangs = {gngQuay, gngStack}
    Opening = 2
    MaxStake = 2

INVARIANT CreditsConserved
PROPERTY CreditsEventuallySpent

\* An exhausted credit pool with nothing left to negotiate is quiescent, not
\* deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard funds joint lifts out of a fixed pool of lift credits shared between its crane gangs. Every credit is accounted for at all times: it is either in a gang's own balance, escrowed against a joint lift being negotiated, or already spent on a completed lift. Credits are never minted and never lost.

A joint lift is agreed by two-phase commit. In the voting phase, while no decision stands, an active gang that has not yet voted either commits some of its own credits -- any amount up to the per-gang cap that its balance will cover -- moving them out of its balance and into its escrow, and votes yes; or, if its balance is empty, votes no without moving anything. Once every active gang has voted, the yard decides: commit if every vote was yes, abort otherwise.

In the apply phase, a gang that voted yes acts on the decision. On a commit it moves its escrowed credits into the spent tally; on an abort it moves them back into its own balance. Either way the gang is then marked as having applied.

When a decision stands and no gang is still sitting on an unapplied yes vote, the yard resets for the next negotiation: the decision is cleared, every gang goes back to not having voted, and every escrow is zeroed out. That zeroing is why the reset is only allowed once nobody is still holding escrowed credits.

Capacity changes while the yard is running: the set of gangs active in the negotiation is republished as gangs come on and off shift. The new set may not be empty, and a gang being taken out of the negotiation must not have voted yet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The credits in the gangs' balances, plus the credits held in escrow, plus the credits already spent always add up to exactly the size of the yard's credit pool.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Credits are eventually spent -- some joint lift eventually goes through.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m5p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Sessions, Schedulers, Members, Quorum, DayTotal, MaxAsk,
          MaxRound, NoSession, NoBallot

VARIABLES pool, booked, used, round, bid, ballot

Vars == <<pool, booked, used, round, bid, ballot>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

NoBid == [rnd |-> 0, sess |-> NoSession, mins |-> 0, poolRead |-> 0]

\* Ballots are counted per bid and per round, because a slot can still hold a
\* ballot cast in a round that has since closed.
Backing(s) ==
    Cardinality({m \in Members : ballot[m] # NoBallot
                                 /\ ballot[m].sch = s
                                 /\ ballot[m].rnd = round})

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..(2 * DayTotal) /\ used \in 0..DayTotal
    /\ booked \in [Sessions -> 0..DayTotal] /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ bid \in [Schedulers -> [rnd: 0..MaxRound,
                sess: {NoSession} \union Sessions, mins: 0..MaxAsk,
                poolRead: 0..(2 * DayTotal)]]
    /\ ballot \in [Members -> {NoBallot} \union [sch: Schedulers,
                                                rnd: 0..MaxRound]]

Init ==
    /\ pool = DayTotal /\ used = 0
    /\ booked = [s \in Sessions |-> 0] /\ round = 0
    /\ bid = [s \in Schedulers |-> NoBid]
    /\ ballot = [m \in Members |-> NoBallot]

PutBid(s, t, n) ==
    /\ bid[s].sess = NoSession /\ n <= pool
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![s] = [rnd |-> round, sess |-> t, mins |-> n,
                                  poolRead |-> pool]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, ballot>>

CastBallot(m, s) ==
    /\ ballot[m] = NoBallot /\ bid[s].sess # NoSession
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = [sch |-> s, rnd |-> bid[s].rnd]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, bid>>

\* The pool is written back from the reading on the bid, so the round test is
\* what keeps that reading true.
Enact(s) ==
    /\ bid[s].sess # NoSession /\ bid[s].rnd = round
    /\ Backing(s) >= Quorum /\ bid[s].mins <= bid[s].poolRead
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![bid[s].sess] = @ + bid[s].mins]
    /\ pool' = bid[s].poolRead - bid[s].mins
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![s] = NoBid]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, ballot>>

Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ bid[s].sess # NoSession /\ bid[s].rnd # round
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![s] = NoBid]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, ballot>>

ClearBallot(m) ==
    /\ ballot[m] # NoBallot /\ ballot[m].rnd # round
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = NoBallot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, booked, used, round, bid>>

UseMinute(t) ==
    /\ booked[t] > 0 /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
    /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, round, bid, ballot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers, t \in Sessions, n \in 1..MaxAsk : PutBid(s, t, n)
    \/ \E m \in Members, s \in Schedulers : CastBallot(m, s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Enact(s) \/ Withdraw(s)
    \/ \E m \in Members : ClearBallot(m)
    \/ \E t \in Sessions : UseMinute(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: pool plus bookings plus used minutes is always exactly the
\* day's total, so no enactment mints or loses a theatre minute.
MinutesConserved == pool + Tally(booked, Sessions) + used = DayTotal
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Sessions = {sesOrtho, sesCardio}
    Schedulers = {schDay, schTwilight}
    Members = {memChair, memAnaes}
    Quorum = 2
    DayTotal = 2
    MaxAsk = 1
    MaxRound = 2
    NoSession = nosession
    NoBallot = noballot

INVARIANT MinutesConserved

\* With the round budget spent and the day's minutes used the schedule is
\* quiescent, which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital allocates its operating-theatre minutes for the day out of one pool. Every minute is accounted for: it is either unallocated in the pool, booked against a particular session, or already used. Minutes are never invented and never lost.

Nothing is allocated on one person's say-so. Each reallocation needs a quorum of the scheduling committee, and the scheduler works in rounds: there is a round number, and it advances every time an allocation is enacted.

Either of two schedulers may put a bid on the table. A bid names a session, names how many minutes it wants, records the round number in force, and records the pool figure the scheduler read at that moment. A scheduler may only have one bid on the table at a time.

Committee members vote by ballot. Each member has one ballot slot, and a member with an empty slot may place a ballot naming a bid and the round that bid was made in. Ballots do not arrive in the order they were cast and are counted and cleared independently, so a slot can still be holding a ballot for a round that has since closed.

Enacting a bid requires that the bid's round is still the round in force, that the ballots for that bid in the round in force reach quorum, and that the minutes asked for do not exceed the pool figure recorded on the bid. Enacting adds those minutes to the session's booking, writes the pool back as the figure recorded on the bid minus the minutes taken -- an absolute value derived from the old reading -- advances the round, and clears the bid off the table.

A bid whose round has closed is withdrawn. A ballot whose round has closed may be cleared out of its slot. And any session with minutes booked against it may use one of them, which moves that minute into the used tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The minutes unallocated in the pool, plus the minutes booked against all sessions, plus the minutes already used always add up to exactly the day's total theatre minutes.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m1p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, Deals, MaxLap, NoPost

Banks == 0..(RingSize - 1)

Onward(b) == (b + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES tokenAt, lap, recalls, lastPost, stage, refused

Vars == <<tokenAt, lap, recalls, lastPost, stage, refused>>

\* `recalls[b]` is the lap b was told when it took the token, and nothing ever
\* corrects it, so a bank the supervisor went around still trusts it.
Current(b) == recalls[b] = lap

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokenAt \in Banks /\ lap \in 0..MaxLap
    /\ recalls \in [Banks -> 0..MaxLap]
    /\ lastPost \in {NoPost} \union [bank: Banks, lp: 0..MaxLap]
    /\ stage \in [Deals -> {"open", "debited", "settled"}]
    /\ refused \subseteq Banks

Init ==
    /\ tokenAt = 0 /\ lap = 1
    /\ recalls = [b \in Banks |-> IF b = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ lastPost = NoPost
    /\ stage = [d \in Deals |-> "open"]
    /\ refused = {}

HandOn(b) ==
    /\ tokenAt = b /\ lap < MaxLap
    /\ tokenAt' = Onward(b) /\ lap' = lap + 1
    /\ recalls' = [recalls EXCEPT ![Onward(b)] = lap + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lastPost, stage, refused>>

\* The supervisor says nothing to the bank it took the token from.
Recall(c) ==
    /\ c # tokenAt /\ lap < MaxLap
    /\ tokenAt' = c /\ lap' = lap + 1
    /\ recalls' = [recalls EXCEPT ![c] = lap + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lastPost, stage, refused>>

\* The journal does the stamping, with the lap in force when the posting
\* lands -- not with the lap the posting bank remembers.
PostDebit(b, d) ==
    /\ Current(b) /\ stage[d] = "open"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d] = "debited"]
    /\ lastPost' = [bank |-> b, lp |-> lap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, lap, recalls, refused>>

PostCredit(b, d) ==
    /\ Current(b) /\ stage[d] = "debited"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d] = "settled"]
    /\ lastPost' = [bank |-> b, lp |-> lap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, lap, recalls, refused>>

Refuse(b) ==
    /\ ~Current(b) /\ b \notin refused
    /\ refused' = refused \union {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, lap, recalls, lastPost, stage>>

PostStep == \E b \in Banks, d \in Deals : PostDebit(b, d) \/ PostCredit(b, d)

Next ==
    \/ PostStep
    \/ \E b \in Banks : HandOn(b) \/ Recall(b) \/ Refuse(b)

\* Whoever holds the token always has the lap in force recorded, so a posting
\* step is always available while any deal is unfinished.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(PostStep)

\* No stale participant acts: a posting stamped with the lap now in force can
\* only have come from the bank that now holds the token.
FrontOfJournalIsCurrent ==
    (lastPost # NoPost /\ lastPost.lp = lap) => lastPost.bank = tokenAt

\* Progress: every deal is posted right through.
AllDealsSettled == <>(\A d \in Deals : stage[d] = "settled")
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Deals = {dlGilt, dlSwap}
    MaxLap = 4
    NoPost = nopost

INVARIANT FrontOfJournalIsCurrent
PROPERTY AllDealsSettled

\* Every deal settled with the lap budget spent is the end of the session,
\* not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A clearing house lets its member banks post to the settlement journal one at a time. The right to post circulates as a ring token, and the ring register holds both which bank has the token and a lap number that advances every time the token moves. Each bank separately remembers the lap number it was given when it received the token, and nothing ever corrects that memory. The session opens on lap one, with the first bank holding the token and no other bank remembering any lap at all.

The journal, not the bank, does the stamping: every posting is written into the journal stamped with the lap number in force at the moment it lands, together with the bank it came from. Only the most recent posting is kept on the front of the journal for reconciliation.

A bank holding the token may hand it on to the next bank around the ring, which advances the lap and tells the receiving bank its new lap number. Banks are slow but they do not fail: one may sit on the token for a long time and will still eventually act. Because of that, the clearing supervisor can recall the token from a slow bank and give it directly to any other bank, which also advances the lap and tells the receiving bank its new lap number -- but says nothing at all to the bank it was taken from, which carries on believing the lap it remembers is the lap in force.

Each settlement deal is posted in two stages, a debit then a credit. A bank whose remembered lap equals the lap in force may post the debit stage of an open deal, or the credit stage of a deal already debited, and the deal advances accordingly. A bank whose remembered lap does not equal the lap in force is refused and noted in the refusals log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: If the most recent posting in the journal was stamped with the lap number now in force, then it came from the bank that now holds the ring token.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every settlement deal is eventually fully posted, debit and credit.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bays, Volume, Draw

VARIABLES tank, charged, drained, ready, voting, inService

Vars == <<tank, charged, drained, ready, voting, inService>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ tank \in 0..(2 * Volume) /\ drained \in 0..Volume
    /\ charged \in [Bays -> 0..Draw]
    /\ ready \subseteq Bays /\ voting \in BOOLEAN
    /\ inService \subseteq Bays

Init ==
    /\ tank = Volume /\ drained = 0
    /\ charged = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ ready = {} /\ voting = FALSE /\ inService = Bays

\* Opening a round clears the ready set, because an aborted round leaves the
\* old votes standing and the commit writes lines absolutely.
OpenRound ==
    /\ ~voting /\ inService # {}
    /\ voting' = TRUE /\ ready' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, inService>>

VoteReady(b) ==
    /\ voting /\ b \in inService /\ b \notin ready /\ charged[b] = 0
    /\ ready' = ready \union {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, voting, inService>>

\* One write fills every ready bay's line to its full draw.
Commit ==
    /\ voting /\ ready = inService
    /\ tank >= Draw * Cardinality(ready)
    /\ charged' = [b \in Bays |-> IF b \in ready THEN Draw ELSE charged[b]]
    /\ tank' = tank - Draw * Cardinality(ready)
    /\ voting' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drained, ready, inService>>

Abort ==
    /\ voting /\ voting' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, ready, inService>>

Reclaim(b) ==
    /\ charged[b] > 0
    /\ charged' = [charged EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1] /\ tank' = tank + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drained, ready, voting, inService>>

Discharge(b) ==
    /\ charged[b] > 0
    /\ charged' = [charged EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1] /\ drained' = drained + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, ready, voting, inService>>

\* Capacity changes between rounds, never inside one.
Republish(bs) ==
    /\ ~voting /\ bs # {} /\ inService' = bs
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tank, charged, drained, ready, voting>>

Next ==
    \/ OpenRound \/ Commit \/ Abort
    \/ \E b \in Bays : VoteReady(b) \/ Reclaim(b) \/ Discharge(b)
    \/ \E bs \in SUBSET Bays : Republish(bs)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: tank plus charged lines plus drained is always exactly the
\* volume the plant holds, so no commit writes over water already in a line.
WaterConserved == tank + Tally(charged, Bays) + drained = Volume
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Bays = {byArch, byBrush, byBlow}
    Volume = 3
    Draw = 1

INVARIANT WaterConserved

\* An empty plant with everything drained is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car wash recycles its water. Every litre in the system is accounted for: it is sitting in the reclaim tank, charged into one of the bays' spray lines, or already discharged to the drain. Litres are never created and never lost.

Charging the bays is done as a two-phase commit, because a bay charged while another bay is not ready sprays into an empty stall. In the voting phase the plant opens a round and each in-service bay with an empty spray line may vote itself ready. The round is committed only when every in-service bay has voted ready and the reclaim tank holds enough water to charge them all: committing fills the spray line of every bay in the ready set to its full draw in one write, takes that many litres out of the tank, and closes the round. A round may also simply be aborted, which closes it without charging anything.

Opening a round clears the ready set first. That matters because aborting a round leaves the ready set as it was, so without the clear a bay could still be counted ready in a later round when its line is no longer empty -- and the commit fills lines to their full draw as an absolute write rather than topping them up, so a bay counted ready with water already in it would have that water written over.

Water leaves a bay in one of two ways: a bay with water in its line may return one litre to the reclaim tank, or may discharge one litre to the drain.

Capacity changes while the plant is running: the set of in-service bays is republished between rounds as bays are opened and closed for maintenance. The new set may not be empty, and it may only be republished while no round is open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The water in the reclaim tank, plus the water charged into the bays' spray lines, plus the water already discharged to the drain always adds up to exactly the volume the system holds.

---- MODULE W4Od12m5p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Docs, Units, Quorum, MaxRound, NoWork

Signoff == [doc: Docs, rnd: 0..MaxRound]

VARIABLES panelRound, panel, sheet, inHand, state

Vars == <<panelRound, panel, sheet, inHand, state>>

AlreadyOn(d, u) == \E s \in sheet[u] : s.doc = d

TypeOK ==
    /\ panelRound \in 0..MaxRound /\ panel \subseteq Docs
    /\ sheet \in [Units -> SUBSET Signoff]
    /\ inHand \in [Docs -> {NoWork} \union [unit: Units, rnd: 0..MaxRound]]
    /\ state \in [Units -> {"held", "released"}]

Init ==
    /\ panelRound = 0 /\ panel = Docs
    /\ sheet = [u \in Units |-> {}]
    /\ inHand = [d \in Docs |-> NoWork]
    /\ state = [u \in Units |-> "held"]

\* Wiping the sheets is part of reconstituting the panel: a sign-off made
\* against an old panel is not evidence about the blood under this one.
Reconstitute(ps) ==
    /\ Cardinality(ps) >= Quorum /\ panelRound < MaxRound
    /\ panel' = ps /\ panelRound' = panelRound + 1
    /\ sheet' = [u \in Units |-> {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inHand, state>>

\* Starting stamps the round in force; the member then goes away for as long
\* as the cross-match takes.
StartSignoff(d, u) ==
    /\ d \in panel /\ inHand[d] = NoWork
    /\ state[u] = "held" /\ ~AlreadyOn(d, u)
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![d] = [unit |-> u, rnd |-> panelRound]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<panelRound, panel, sheet, state>>

LandSignoff(d) ==
    /\ inHand[d] # NoWork /\ inHand[d].rnd = panelRound
    /\ sheet' = [sheet EXCEPT ![inHand[d].unit] =
                    @ \union {[doc |-> d, rnd |-> inHand[d].rnd]}]
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![d] = NoWork]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<panelRound, panel, state>>

\* Not a failure: the member drops the work and will pick something else up.
DropWork(d) ==
    /\ inHand[d] # NoWork /\ inHand[d].rnd # panelRound
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![d] = NoWork]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<panelRound, panel, sheet, state>>

Release(u) ==
    /\ state[u] = "held" /\ Cardinality(sheet[u]) >= Quorum
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![u] = "released"]
    /\ sheet' = [sheet EXCEPT ![u] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<panelRound, panel, inHand>>

PanelStep ==
    \/ \E d \in Docs, u \in Units : StartSignoff(d, u)
    \/ \E d \in Docs : LandSignoff(d) \/ DropWork(d)
    \/ \E u \in Units : Release(u)

Next == PanelStep \/ (\E ps \in SUBSET Docs : Reconstitute(ps))

\* Panel churn is bounded by the round budget, so weak fairness on the panel
\* work is enough once the panel settles.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(PanelStep)

\* No stale participant's word counts: every sign-off on any sheet carries
\* the panel round currently in force.
SheetsAreCurrent ==
    \A u \in Units : \A s \in sheet[u] : s.rnd = panelRound

\* Progress: held units do not sit unreleased forever.
AllUnitsReleased == <>(\A u \in Units : state[u] = "released")
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Docs = {docHaem, docLab, docReg}
    Units = {unRhPos, unRhNeg}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxRound = 2
    NoWork = nowork

INVARIANT SheetsAreCurrent
PROPERTY AllUnitsReleased

\* Every unit released with the round budget spent is the end of the run,
\* not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood bank will not release a unit for transfusion on one person's word. Each unit carries a cross-match sheet, and a unit is released only when its sheet holds a quorum of sign-offs from the cross-match panel.

The panel itself is reconstituted from time to time: a new panel is named, which advances the panel round. A new panel may not be smaller than quorum size. Reconstituting the panel also wipes every unit's cross-match sheet clean, because a sign-off made against an old panel is not evidence about the blood under the panel that exists now.

Haematologists are slow but they do not fail. A panel member with nothing in hand may start a sign-off on a unit still being held, as long as that member is not already down on that unit's sheet; starting stamps the sign-off with the panel round in force at that moment. The member then goes away and does the actual cross-match, which takes as long as it takes, and comes back to land the sign-off on the sheet.

A sign-off only lands if the round stamped on it when it was started is still the round in force. A member that comes back to find the round has moved on drops the work it was carrying instead; it has not failed and will pick something else up.

A unit whose sheet holds at least a quorum of sign-offs is released for transfusion, and its sheet is cleared as the paperwork goes with the unit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every sign-off sitting on any unit's cross-match sheet is stamped with the panel round currently in force.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every unit being held is eventually released for transfusion.

---- MODULE W4Od5m1p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS InstanceCount, Codes, RunSize, MaxSeq, NoCode

Instances == 0..(InstanceCount - 1)

Onward(i) == (i + 1) % InstanceCount

VARIABLES tokenAt, tokenSeq, inHand, burnt, slotsLeft

Vars == <<tokenAt, tokenSeq, inHand, burnt, slotsLeft>>

Empty == [code |-> NoCode, slotsRead |-> 0, seq |-> 0]

\* An instance's recorded sequence number is what ties the slot figure it read
\* to the token it was holding when it read it.
Fresh(i) == inHand[i].seq = tokenSeq

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokenAt \in Instances /\ tokenSeq \in 0..MaxSeq
    /\ inHand \in [Instances -> [code: {NoCode} \union Codes,
                   slotsRead: 0..RunSize, seq: 0..MaxSeq]]
    /\ burnt \subseteq Codes /\ slotsLeft \in 0..RunSize

Init ==
    /\ tokenAt = 0 /\ tokenSeq = 0
    /\ inHand = [i \in Instances |-> Empty]
    /\ burnt = {} /\ slotsLeft = RunSize

PassToken(i) ==
    /\ tokenAt = i /\ tokenSeq < MaxSeq
    /\ tokenAt' = Onward(i) /\ tokenSeq' = tokenSeq + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inHand, burnt, slotsLeft>>

Reserve(i, c) ==
    /\ tokenAt = i /\ inHand[i].code = NoCode
    /\ c \notin burnt /\ slotsLeft > 0
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![i] = [code |-> c, slotsRead |-> slotsLeft,
                                        seq |-> tokenSeq]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, tokenSeq, burnt, slotsLeft>>

\* Irreversible, and the slot figure is written back from the old reading, so
\* the sequence test is what makes that reading still true.
Burn(i) ==
    /\ tokenAt = i /\ inHand[i].code # NoCode /\ Fresh(i)
    /\ inHand[i].slotsRead > 0
    /\ slotsLeft' = inHand[i].slotsRead - 1
    /\ burnt' = burnt \union {inHand[i].code}
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![i] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, tokenSeq>>

Abandon(i) ==
    /\ inHand[i].code # NoCode /\ ~Fresh(i)
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![i] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, tokenSeq, burnt, slotsLeft>>

Decline(i) ==
    /\ tokenAt = i /\ inHand[i].code \in burnt
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![i] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, tokenSeq, burnt, slotsLeft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : PassToken(i) \/ Burn(i) \/ Abandon(i) \/ Decline(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Codes : Reserve(i, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Irreversibility as an accounting identity: slots left plus codes burnt is
\* always the size of the founder run, so no code is burnt twice.
RunFullyAccounted == slotsLeft + Cardinality(burnt) = RunSize
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    InstanceCount = 2
    Codes = {cdAlfa, cdBravo, cdCharlie}
    RunSize = 3
    MaxSeq = 3
    NoCode = nocode

INVARIANT RunFullyAccounted

\* With the token's sequence budget spent the pair is quiescent, which is not
\* a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game gives out a limited run of founder lobby slots. A player claims one by redeeming a single-use invite code. Redeeming is irreversible: once a code is burnt it can never be un-burnt, and the founder slot it consumed can never be handed back. The run of founder slots is fixed, so the slots still unclaimed plus the codes already burnt must always add up to the size of the run.

Two independently deployed matchmaker instances handle redemptions, brought up in different regions and sharing one pool of founder slots. They never talk to each other. The right to burn a code circulates between them as a ring token, and the token carries a sequence number that advances every time the token moves.

An instance holding the token, with nothing already in hand, may reserve a code that has not been burnt, provided there is at least one founder slot left. Reserving records the code, the number of founder slots the instance read at that moment, and the token's sequence number as it stood.

Burning is the irreversible step. An instance may burn what it has in hand only if it holds the token and the sequence number it recorded is still the token's sequence number. Burning writes the remaining founder slots back as the figure the instance read minus one -- an absolute value derived from that old reading, not a decrement of the current figure -- and adds the code to the burnt list.

An instance whose recorded sequence number is no longer the token's abandons what it had in hand. An instance holding the token that finds the code in its hand has already been burnt declines it and puts it down.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The founder slots still unclaimed plus the number of invite codes already burnt always add up to exactly the size of the founder run, so no code is ever burnt twice.

---- MODULE W4Od17m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Terminals, Numbers, Bags, Ctls, NoCtl, NoFlight, NoBag

Flights == Terminals \X Numbers

TerminalOf(f) == f[1]

VARIABLES record, audit, termHandle, fltHandle, work

Vars == <<record, audit, termHandle, fltHandle, work>>

Routed == UNION {audit[f] : f \in Flights}

Blank == [flt |-> NoFlight, bag |-> NoBag, snap |-> {}]

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in [Flights -> SUBSET Bags]
    /\ audit \in [Flights -> SUBSET Bags]
    /\ termHandle \in [Terminals -> {NoCtl} \union Ctls]
    /\ fltHandle \in [Flights -> {NoCtl} \union Ctls]
    /\ work \in [Ctls -> [flt: {NoFlight} \union Flights,
                 bag: {NoBag} \union Bags, snap: SUBSET Bags]]

Init ==
    /\ record = [f \in Flights |-> {}] /\ audit = [f \in Flights |-> {}]
    /\ termHandle = [t \in Terminals |-> NoCtl]
    /\ fltHandle = [f \in Flights |-> NoCtl]
    /\ work = [c \in Ctls |-> Blank]

ClaimTerminal(c, t) ==
    /\ termHandle[t] = NoCtl /\ \A u \in Terminals : termHandle[u] # c
    /\ termHandle' = [termHandle EXCEPT ![t] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, audit, fltHandle, work>>

ReleaseTerminal(c, t) ==
    /\ termHandle[t] = c /\ work[c].flt = NoFlight
    /\ termHandle' = [termHandle EXCEPT ![t] = NoCtl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, audit, fltHandle, work>>

\* Coarse before fine, and claiming the fine handle is also when the whole
\* load record is copied.
ClaimFlight(c, f, b) ==
    /\ termHandle[TerminalOf(f)] = c /\ fltHandle[f] = NoCtl
    /\ work[c].flt = NoFlight /\ b \notin Routed
    /\ fltHandle' = [fltHandle EXCEPT ![f] = c]
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![c] = [flt |-> f, bag |-> b, snap |-> record[f]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, audit, termHandle>>

\* The record is written back wholesale from the copy, which is why the fine
\* handle has to be held right across the read and the write.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ work[c].flt # NoFlight /\ fltHandle[work[c].flt] = c
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![work[c].flt] = work[c].snap
                                                \union {work[c].bag}]
    /\ audit' = [audit EXCEPT ![work[c].flt] = @ \union {work[c].bag}]
    /\ fltHandle' = [fltHandle EXCEPT ![work[c].flt] = NoCtl]
    /\ termHandle' = [termHandle EXCEPT
                          ![TerminalOf(work[c].flt)] = NoCtl]
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![c] = Blank]

Abandon(c) ==
    /\ work[c].flt # NoFlight
    /\ fltHandle' = [fltHandle EXCEPT ![work[c].flt] = NoCtl]
    /\ termHandle' = [termHandle EXCEPT
                          ![TerminalOf(work[c].flt)] = NoCtl]
    /\ work' = [work EXCEPT ![c] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, audit>>

ClaimFlightStep == \E c \in Ctls, f \in Flights, b \in Bags : ClaimFlight(c, f, b)

CommitStep == \E c \in Ctls : Commit(c)

RouteStep ==
    \/ ClaimFlightStep \/ CommitStep
    \/ \E c \in Ctls, t \in Terminals : ClaimTerminal(c, t) \/ ReleaseTerminal(c, t)
    \/ \E c \in Ctls : Abandon(c)

Next == RouteStep

\* Terminal handles can be taken and given back forever, so claiming a flight
\* and committing need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(RouteStep) /\ SF_Vars(ClaimFlightStep) /\ SF_Vars(CommitStep)

\* No lost updates: nothing in a flight's committed-routings audit has been
\* written back out of the flight's load record.
NoRoutingLost == \A f \in Flights : audit[f] \subseteq record[f]

\* Progress: every bag ends up on a flight.
AllBagsRouted == <>(Routed = Bags)
====
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps one shared load record per flight, listing which bags are going on that flight. Two independently deployed routing controllers work over the same pool of flight records; they were commissioned by different handling agents and never coordinate directly. Alongside each flight's load record there is a committed-routings audit for the flight, written one bag at a time and never rewritten wholesale.

Every flight belongs to exactly one terminal, so the controllers take the two levels of entitlement in order, coarse then fine. A controller holding no terminal handle may claim a free terminal handle, and may give a free-standing terminal handle back when it has no work in progress.

Holding a terminal handle and with no work in progress, a controller may claim the handle of a flight in that terminal, provided that flight handle is free and there is a bag not yet routed to any flight at all. Claiming is also when the controller takes its reading: it copies the flight's whole load record as it stands, and remembers the bag it intends to add.

Committing writes the load record back as the copy the controller took plus the one bag it is adding -- the whole record, written wholesale from the reading -- and separately appends that bag to the flight's committed-routings audit. Both handles are then given back. Notice that the wholesale write is what makes the fine handle matter: it must be held right across the read and the write, or a bag added in between is written straight back out of the record.

A controller may instead abandon its work in progress, giving both handles back and writing nothing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every flight, every bag in that flight's committed-routings audit is still present in the flight's load record.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag is eventually routed to some flight.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Gangs, Slots, MaxVer, MaxOverride, NoSlot

VARIABLES plan, ledger, planVer, txn, vote, overrides

Vars == <<plan, ledger, planVer, txn, vote, overrides>>

Idle == [phase |-> "idle", item |-> NoSlot, snap |-> <<>>, ver |-> 0]

AllYes == \A g \in Gangs : vote[g] = "yes"

TypeOK ==
    /\ plan \in Seq(Slots) /\ ledger \in Seq(Slots)
    /\ planVer \in 0..MaxVer /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverride
    /\ txn \in [phase: {"idle", "voting"}, item: {NoSlot} \union Slots,
                snap: Seq(Slots), ver: 0..MaxVer]
    /\ vote \in [Gangs -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]

Init ==
    /\ plan = <<>> /\ ledger = <<>>
    /\ planVer = 0 /\ overrides = 0
    /\ txn = Idle
    /\ vote = [g \in Gangs |-> "none"]

\* Opening copies the whole plan and the version it went with.
OpenTxn(s) ==
    /\ txn.phase = "idle"
    /\ txn' = [phase |-> "voting", item |-> s, snap |-> plan, ver |-> planVer]
    /\ vote' = [g \in Gangs |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, ledger, planVer, overrides>>

CastVote(g, v) ==
    /\ txn.phase = "voting" /\ vote[g] = "none"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![g] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, ledger, planVer, txn, overrides>>

\* The plan is written back wholesale from the copy, so the version test is
\* what stops an amendment landing in between being written straight out.
Commit ==
    /\ txn.phase = "voting" /\ AllYes
    /\ txn.ver = planVer /\ planVer < MaxVer
    /\ plan' = Append(txn.snap, txn.item)
    /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, txn.item)
    /\ planVer' = planVer + 1
    /\ txn' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, overrides>>

Abort ==
    /\ txn.phase = "voting"
    /\ \/ \E g \in Gangs : vote[g] = "no"
       \/ txn.ver # planVer
    /\ txn' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, ledger, planVer, vote, overrides>>

\* The superintendent's privileged path: no transaction, no votes.
SuperintendentAmend(s) ==
    /\ planVer < MaxVer /\ overrides < MaxOverride
    /\ plan' = Append(plan, s) /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, s)
    /\ planVer' = planVer + 1 /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, vote>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots : OpenTxn(s) \/ SuperintendentAmend(s)
    \/ \E g \in Gangs, v \in {"yes", "no"} : CastVote(g, v)
    \/ Commit \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No lost updates: the ledger is a prefix of the plan, so nothing that was
\* agreed has been written back out of the plan.
LedgerIsPrefixOfPlan ==
    /\ Len(ledger) <= Len(plan)
    /\ \A i \in 1..Len(ledger) : plan[i] = ledger[i]
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Gangs = {gngQuay, gngLash}
    Slots = {slBay03, slBay07}
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxOverride = 2
    NoSlot = noslot

INVARIANT LedgerIsPrefixOfPlan

\* With the plan's version budget spent the vessel is closed out, which is not
\* a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard keeps one shared stowage plan for the vessel alongside: an ordered list of the stowage positions that have been agreed, in the order they were agreed. Beside it sits an accepted-amendments ledger, also an ordered list, appended to one entry at a time and never rewritten. The ledger is the record of what was actually agreed, so the plan must always begin with exactly the ledger.

Amendments are agreed by two-phase commit across the crane gangs. Opening a transaction names the position to be added and takes a copy of the whole plan as it stands together with the plan's version number; every gang's vote is reset to not-yet-cast. In the voting phase each gang casts a yes or a no. The transaction commits only if every gang voted yes and the plan's version number is still the number recorded when the transaction opened; committing writes the plan back as the copy taken at opening with the new position appended, appends that position to the ledger, and advances the plan's version. A transaction is aborted if any gang voted no or if the plan's version has moved on.

The version check at commit time is doing real work, because the plan is written back wholesale from the copy taken at opening rather than appended to in place.

The yard superintendent has a privileged override: a position can be appended to the plan and to the ledger directly, with no transaction and no votes, which also advances the plan's version. The superintendent's amendments are counted in the override register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The plan always begins with exactly the accepted-amendments ledger -- the ledger's entries appear at the front of the plan, in the same order, so no agreed amendment is ever written back out of the plan.

---- MODULE W4Od18m3p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Hubs, Doors, MaxTerm, NoHub

VARIABLES term, coord, grant, transmitting, locked, promotions

Vars == <<term, coord, grant, transmitting, locked, promotions>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm /\ coord \in {NoHub} \union Hubs
    /\ grant \in [Hubs -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ transmitting \subseteq Hubs /\ locked \subseteq Doors
    /\ promotions \subseteq Hubs

\* The network opens on term one so that a hub holding no grant at all cannot
\* be mistaken for a hub granted the term in force.
Init ==
    /\ term = 1 /\ coord = NoHub
    /\ grant = [h \in Hubs |-> 0]
    /\ transmitting = {} /\ locked = {} /\ promotions = {}

\* An orderly election waits for the channel to go quiet.
Elect(h) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm /\ coord # h /\ transmitting = {}
    /\ term' = term + 1 /\ coord' = h
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![h] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transmitting, locked, promotions>>

\* The privileged path does not wait, so it must clear the channel: the
\* promotion has just made every other grant out of date.
Promote(h) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm /\ coord # h
    /\ term' = term + 1 /\ coord' = h
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![h] = term + 1]
    /\ transmitting' = {}
    /\ promotions' = promotions \union {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED locked

BeginTransmit(h) ==
    /\ grant[h] = term /\ h \notin transmitting
    /\ transmitting' = transmitting \union {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, coord, grant, locked, promotions>>

SendLock(h, d) ==
    /\ h \in transmitting /\ d \notin locked
    /\ transmitting' = transmitting \ {h}
    /\ locked' = locked \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, coord, grant, promotions>>

StopTransmit(h) ==
    /\ h \in transmitting
    /\ transmitting' = transmitting \ {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, coord, grant, locked, promotions>>

ElectStep == \E h \in Hubs : Elect(h)

SendStep == \E h \in Hubs, d \in Doors : SendLock(h, d)

HubStep == SendStep \/ (\E h \in Hubs : BeginTransmit(h) \/ StopTransmit(h))

Next == ElectStep \/ HubStep \/ (\E h \in Hubs : Promote(h))

\* A hub can go on and off the channel without sending anything, so the send
\* step needs strong fairness to get a foot in that churn; promotions are
\* bounded by the term budget.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(ElectStep) /\ WF_Vars(HubStep) /\ SF_Vars(SendStep)

\* Mutual exclusion of the radio channel: a transmitting hub is the recorded
\* coordinator holding a grant stamped with the term in force, and the record
\* names at most one hub.
ChannelHeldUnderLiveGrant ==
    \A h \in transmitting : grant[h] = term /\ coord = h

\* Progress: the house really does get locked up.
AllDoorsLocked == <>(locked = Doors)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Hubs = {hubHall, hubGarage, hubLoft}
    Doors = {drFront, drPatio}
    MaxTerm = 4
    NoHub = nohub

INVARIANT ChannelHeldUnderLiveGrant
PROPERTY AllDoorsLocked

\* Every door locked with the term budget spent is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network is driven by several hubs sharing one low-power radio channel. The channel is the critical resource: exactly one hub may be transmitting on it at any instant, or the lock commands collide and doors are left in an unknown state.

The right to transmit is held by an elected coordinator. The network keeps a term number, the identity of the coordinator, and a transmit grant per hub stamped with the term that grant was issued in. The network opens on term one with no coordinator elected and no hub holding a grant.

An election may be called for any hub that is not already the coordinator, but only while the channel is quiet: the term advances, that hub becomes coordinator, and its transmit grant is stamped with the new term. A hub may begin transmitting if its grant is stamped with the term now in force and it is not already transmitting. A transmitting hub finishes by sending the lock command for a door that is not yet locked, which records that door as locked and takes the hub off the channel. A transmitting hub may also come off the channel without sending anything at all.

The homeowner has a privileged override that does not wait for the channel to go quiet: any hub that is not the coordinator can be promoted on the spot. The term advances, that hub becomes coordinator with a grant stamped with the new term, the promotion is noted in the override register, and the channel is cleared -- whatever was transmitting is cut off. Clearing the channel is essential, because the promotion has just made every other grant out of date and a hub left transmitting under an old grant is exactly the collision the network is trying to avoid.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any hub transmitting on the radio channel holds a grant stamped with the term now in force and is the hub currently recorded as coordinator.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every door in the network is eventually locked.

---- MODULE W4Od12m6p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Fridges, Porters, Stock, TrolleyCap, Span, NoPorter

VARIABLES fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed

Vars == <<fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

Running(p) == p \notin crashed

Working(p) == lease.holder = p /\ lease.ticks > 0

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridge \in [Fridges -> 0..Stock] /\ transfused \in 0..Stock
    /\ trolley \in [Porters -> 0..TrolleyCap] /\ quarantined \in 0..Stock
    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoPorter} \union Porters, ticks: 0..Span]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Porters

Init ==
    /\ fridge = [f \in Fridges |-> IF f = CHOOSE g \in Fridges : TRUE
                                   THEN Stock ELSE 0]
    /\ trolley = [p \in Porters |-> 0]
    /\ transfused = 0 /\ quarantined = 0
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoPorter, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

Tick ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, crashed>>

\* The hand-over has to account for whatever the outgoing porter was carrying:
\* those units cannot go back to a fridge, but they cannot vanish either.
TakeLease(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ (lease.holder = NoPorter \/ lease.ticks = 0)
    /\ trolley' = IF lease.holder = NoPorter THEN trolley
                  ELSE [trolley EXCEPT ![lease.holder] = 0]
    /\ quarantined' = IF lease.holder = NoPorter THEN quarantined
                      ELSE quarantined + trolley[lease.holder]
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> p, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, transfused, crashed>>

Collect(p, f) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ Working(p)
    /\ fridge[f] > 0 /\ trolley[p] < TrolleyCap
    /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

Shelve(p, f) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ Working(p) /\ trolley[p] > 0
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![p] = @ - 1]
    /\ fridge' = [fridge EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transfused, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

Transfuse(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ Working(p) /\ trolley[p] > 0
    /\ trolley' = [trolley EXCEPT ![p] = @ - 1]
    /\ transfused' = transfused + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, quarantined, lease, crashed>>

\* Silent: the trolley stays loaded, the lease stays held, nothing is said.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, trolley, transfused, quarantined, lease>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E p \in Porters : TakeLease(p) \/ Transfuse(p) \/ Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Porters, f \in Fridges : Collect(p, f) \/ Shelve(p, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Conservation: fridges plus trolleys plus transfused plus quarantined is
\* always exactly the opening stock, so a hand-over never loses a unit.
StockFullyAccounted ==
    Tally(fridge, Fridges) + Tally(trolley, Porters)
        + transfused + quarantined = Stock
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Fridges = {frMain, frSatellite}
    Porters = {ptDay, ptNight}
    Stock = 3
    TrolleyCap = 2
    Span = 2
    NoPorter = noporter

INVARIANT StockFullyAccounted

\* A fully crashed pair with the lease run down is stuck, which is the outcome
\* being modelled and not a deadlock to report.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood bank tracks every unit it holds. A unit is in one of the fridges, on a porter's trolley, already transfused, or in the quarantine tally. Those four together must always account for exactly the stock the bank opened with: units are never conjured up and, more importantly, never allowed to quietly disappear.

Only one porter at a time may work the master ledger, and the right to do so is a lease with a fixed number of ticks left on it. The lease names its holder and its remaining ticks; a tick of the bank's clock takes one off. A lease with no ticks left has expired.

Any running porter may take the lease when it is unheld or when the current lease has expired. Taking it is also a hand-over of the ledger, and the hand-over has to deal with whatever the outgoing porter was carrying: the outgoing porter's trolley is emptied and everything that was on it goes into the quarantine tally, because units that were in a porter's hands when the ledger changed hands cannot be trusted back into a fridge but must still be accounted for. The new lease then starts with a full complement of ticks.

A running porter holding a lease with ticks left may take one unit out of a fridge onto its trolley if the trolley has room, may put one unit from its trolley back into a fridge, or may transfuse one unit off its trolley, which moves it into the transfused tally.

Any porter can crash silently. A crashed porter stops doing anything at all: it keeps whatever is on its trolley, it keeps the lease if it held one, and nothing is announced. The only thing that recovers the situation is the lease running out of ticks and somebody else taking it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units in the fridges, plus the units on the porters' trolleys, plus the units transfused, plus the units in quarantine always add up to exactly the stock the bank opened with.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Flights, Allocators, MaxCap, MaxEpoch, NoFlight

VARIABLES pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity, draft

Vars == <<pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity, draft>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

Blank == [flt |-> NoFlight, ep |-> 0, poolRead |-> 0]

Quiet == \A a \in Allocators : draft[a].flt = NoFlight

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..(2 * MaxCap) /\ used \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ assigned \in [Flights -> 0..MaxCap]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ draft \in [Allocators -> [flt: {NoFlight} \union Flights,
                  ep: 0..MaxEpoch, poolRead: 0..(2 * MaxCap)]]

Init ==
    /\ pool = MaxCap /\ used = 0
    /\ assigned = [f \in Flights |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0 /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ draft = [a \in Allocators |-> Blank]

\* Republishing moves the difference into or out of the free pool so the books
\* balance, and never leaves the allocator with nothing to hand out.
Republish(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ c >= 1
    /\ pool + c - capacity >= 1
    /\ capacity' = c /\ pool' = pool + c - capacity
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, used, draft>>

\* The book allows one draft at a time.
StartDraft(a, f) ==
    /\ Quiet /\ pool > 0
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![a] = [flt |-> f, ep |-> epoch,
                                      poolRead |-> pool]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity>>

\* The pool is written back from the old reading, so the epoch test is what
\* keeps that reading true across a republish.
Assign(a) ==
    /\ draft[a].flt # NoFlight /\ draft[a].ep = epoch
    /\ draft[a].poolRead > 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![draft[a].flt] = @ + 1]
    /\ pool' = draft[a].poolRead - 1
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![a] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, epoch, capacity>>

Discard(a) ==
    /\ draft[a].flt # NoFlight /\ draft[a].ep # epoch
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![a] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, assigned, used, epoch, capacity>>

UseSlot(f) ==
    /\ assigned[f] > 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1] /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, epoch, capacity, draft>>

AllocStep ==
    \/ \E a \in Allocators, f \in Flights : StartDraft(a, f)
    \/ \E a \in Allocators : Assign(a) \/ Discard(a)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : UseSlot(f)

Next == AllocStep \/ (\E c \in 1..MaxCap : Republish(c))

\* Republishing is bounded by the epoch budget, so weak fairness on the
\* allocation steps carries a slot through once capacity settles.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(AllocStep)

\* Conservation: free pool plus assignments plus used slots is always exactly
\* the capacity published for the hour.
SlotsConserved == pool + Tally(assigned, Flights) + used = capacity

\* Progress: a slot really does get used.
SomeSlotUsed == <>(used > 0)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Flights = {flBA12, flLH80}
    Allocators = {alcNorth, alcSouth}
    MaxCap = 3
    MaxEpoch = 3
    NoFlight = noflight

INVARIANT SlotsConserved
PROPERTY SomeSlotUsed

\* An hour worked off with the epoch budget spent is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport's runway allocator hands out landing slots for the hour. Every slot in the hour's capacity is accounted for: it is unassigned in the free pool, assigned to a particular flight, or already used. Slots are never invented and never lost.

Capacity changes while the hour is running, because runways go in and out of use for weather and works. The capacity figure is republished by a reconfiguration, which carries an epoch number: republishing sets a new capacity, moves the difference into or out of the free pool so that the books still balance, and advances the epoch. Two conditions apply to a republish: the new capacity must be at least one slot, and it must leave at least one slot unassigned in the free pool, so the allocator never reconfigures itself into having nothing to hand out.

Two allocator processes share the slot book, but the book allows only one draft at a time: an allocator may start a draft only when no draft at all is outstanding. Starting a draft names a flight, records the epoch in force, and records the free-pool figure the allocator read at that moment, and requires the pool to be non-empty.

Assigning the draft is only allowed if the epoch recorded on it is still the epoch in force. Assigning adds one slot to the flight's assignment and writes the free pool back as the figure recorded on the draft minus one -- an absolute value derived from the old reading, not a decrement of the pool as it now stands. That is why the epoch test matters: a republish between the reading and the assignment has already moved the pool.

A draft whose epoch has been superseded is discarded. And any flight with a slot assigned to it may use that slot, which moves it into the used tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The slots in the free pool, plus the slots assigned to flights, plus the slots already used always add up to exactly the capacity currently published for the hour.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A landing slot is eventually used -- some flight eventually lands.

    MaxSerial = 3
    NoTech = notech
    NoOrder = noorder

\* With the lease serial budget spent the cabinet is closed out, which is not

nl:
A pharmacy's controlled-drug cabinet is worked under a dispensing lease. The lease names one technician, carries a countdown of ticks left on it, and carries a serial number that is advanced by every change of the lease. Only work done under the lease now in force may be in flight against the cabinet -- an order sitting in flight under a lease that has already gone is an order nobody is answerable for.

A technician may take the lease when it is unheld; taking it advances the serial and starts the countdown at its full span. A tick of the pharmacy clock takes one off the countdown. When the countdown reaches zero the lease is expired outright: the holder is dropped, the serial advances, and every order in flight anywhere is cancelled. Cancelling the orders is the whole point of the expiry: after the serial moves, an order in flight is no longer covered by anything.

The technician holding a lease with ticks left, and with no order of its own already in flight, may cut an order for a prescription that has not been dispensed. The order carries the serial of the lease it was cut under. Dispensing requires that the technician is still the lease holder and that the serial on its order is still the serial in force; dispensing records the prescription as dispensed and takes the order out of flight.

The pharmacist in charge has a privileged override: any undispensed prescription can be dispensed directly, with no lease at all. Doing so seizes the cabinet -- the lease is voided, the serial advances, and every order in flight is cancelled -- and the prescription is noted in the override register.

A technician that is not the lease holder is refused and noted in the refusals log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every order in flight against the cabinet belongs to the technician currently holding the lease and carries the serial number of the lease now in force.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Units == Groups \X Ids

GroupOf(u) == u[1]

VARIABLES state, epoch, policy, slip, charges

Vars == <<state, epoch, policy, slip, charges>>

Ash == {u \in Units : state[u] = "ash"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ state \in [Units -> {"stock", "condemned", "ash"}]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch /\ policy \subseteq Groups
    /\ slip \in [Techs -> {NoSlip} \union [unit: Units, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ charges \in 0..Charges

Init ==
    /\ state = [u \in Units |-> "stock"]
    /\ epoch = 0 /\ policy = Groups
    /\ slip = [t \in Techs |-> NoSlip]
    /\ charges = Charges

Republish(gs) ==
    /\ gs # {} /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ policy' = gs /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, slip, charges>>

WriteSlip(t, u) ==
    /\ slip[t] = NoSlip /\ state[u] = "stock" /\ GroupOf(u) \in policy
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![t] = [unit |-> u, ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![u] = "condemned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, policy, charges>>

\* The slip is not filed here, so the condemned test is what stops one slip
\* drawing two charges out of the canister for a single unit.
Incinerate(t) ==
    /\ slip[t] # NoSlip /\ slip[t].ep = epoch
    /\ state[slip[t].unit] = "condemned" /\ charges > 0
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![slip[t].unit] = "ash"]
    /\ charges' = charges - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, policy, slip>>

FileSlip(t) ==
    /\ slip[t] # NoSlip /\ state[slip[t].unit] = "ash"
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![t] = NoSlip]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, epoch, policy, charges>>

\* The slow technician's slip is superseded; the unit is unharmed and goes
\* back into stock.
VoidSlip(t) ==
    /\ slip[t] # NoSlip /\ slip[t].ep # epoch
    /\ state[slip[t].unit] = "condemned"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![slip[t].unit] = "stock"]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![t] = NoSlip]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, policy, charges>>

BankStep ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs, u \in Units : WriteSlip(t, u)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Incinerate(t) \/ FileSlip(t) \/ VoidSlip(t)

Next == BankStep \/ (\E gs \in SUBSET Groups : Republish(gs))

\* Republishing is bounded by the epoch budget and never blocks the disposal
\* steps, so weak fairness on those carries a unit through.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(BankStep)

\* Irreversibility as an accounting identity: charges left plus units turned
\* to ash is always the canister's capacity, so nothing is burnt twice.
CanisterFullyAccounted == charges + Cardinality(Ash) = Charges

\* Progress: the canister really is drawn on.
SomethingIsIncinerated == <>(charges < Charges)

CONSTANTS
    Groups = {grORh, grABRh}
    Ids = {id1}
    Techs = {tcHalt, tcMori}
    Charges = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoSlip = noslip

INVARIANT CanisterFullyAccounted
PROPERTY SomethingIsIncinerated

\* An empty canister with nothing left in stock is the end of the disposal
\* run, not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood bank disposes of time-expired units by incineration. Incineration is irreversible: a unit that has gone to ash cannot be recovered, and the charge it consumed out of the incinerator's canister cannot be recovered either. The canister holds a fixed number of charges, so the charges left plus the number of units turned to ash must always add up to exactly the canister's capacity -- which is the same as saying no unit is ever incinerated twice.

Which blood groups are for disposal is set by a condemnation policy carrying an epoch number. Republishing the policy names a new, non-empty set of groups for disposal and advances the epoch.

A technician with no slip in hand may write a condemnation slip for a unit that is still in stock and whose group the current policy condemns. The slip records the unit and the epoch in force when it was written, and the unit is marked condemned.

Technicians are slow but they do not fail. A slip may sit in a technician's hand for a long time, and the policy may be republished while it does. Acting on a slip requires that the epoch on it is still the epoch in force, that the unit it names is still merely condemned rather than already ash, and that the canister has a charge left: the unit goes to ash and one charge is consumed. The slip is not filed at that point -- filing is a separate step, allowed once the unit the slip names has gone to ash.

A technician holding a slip whose epoch has been superseded voids it: the unit named goes back into stock and the slip is torn up. The unit has not been harmed; it is simply no longer condemned under the policy that now applies.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The charges left in the incinerator's canister plus the number of units turned to ash always add up to exactly the canister's capacity, so no unit is ever incinerated twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An incineration eventually happens -- the canister is eventually drawn on.

Live(e) == lease.holder = e /\ lease.ticks > 0

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Symbols -> {"open", "closed"}]
    /\ struck \in [Symbols -> 0..MaxPrice]
    /\ tape \in Seq(Symbols)
    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoEngine} \union Engines, ticks: 0..Span]
    /\ prepped \in [Engines -> {NoSymbol} \union Symbols]
    /\ overrides \subseteq Symbols

Init ==
    /\ phase = [s \in Symbols |-> "open"]
    /\ struck = [s \in Symbols |-> 0]
    /\ tape = <<>>
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoEngine, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ prepped = [e \in Engines |-> NoSymbol]
    /\ overrides = {}

TakeLease(e) ==
    /\ lease.holder = NoEngine \/ lease.ticks = 0
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> e, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, struck, tape, prepped, overrides>>

Tick ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, struck, tape, prepped, overrides>>

\* Preparing is the engine's own working state and is never written to the
\* book, so it does not stop anybody else preparing the same symbol.
Prepare(e, s) ==
    /\ Live(e) /\ prepped[e] = NoSymbol /\ phase[s] = "open"
    /\ prepped' = [prepped EXCEPT ![e] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, struck, tape, lease, overrides>>

\* The "still open" test matters: an engine can be left holding a preparation
\* for a symbol somebody else struck while its lease was expired.
Strike(e, p) ==
    /\ Live(e) /\ prepped[e] # NoSymbol
    /\ phase[prepped[e]] = "open" /\ p >= 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![prepped[e]] = "closed"]
    /\ struck' = [struck EXCEPT ![prepped[e]] = p]
    /\ tape' = Append(tape, prepped[e])
    /\ prepped' = [prepped EXCEPT ![e] = NoSymbol]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, overrides>>

Discard(e) ==
    /\ prepped[e] # NoSymbol /\ ~Live(e)
    /\ prepped' = [prepped EXCEPT ![e] = NoSymbol]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, struck, tape, lease, overrides>>

\* The supervisor's privileged path takes no lease at all.
SupervisorStrike(s, p) ==
    /\ phase[s] = "open" /\ p >= 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "closed"]
    /\ struck' = [struck EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ tape' = Append(tape, s)
    /\ overrides' = overrides \union {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, prepped>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E e \in Engines : TakeLease(e) \/ Discard(e)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, s \in Symbols : Prepare(e, s)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, p \in 1..MaxPrice : Strike(e, p)
    \/ \E s \in Symbols, p \in 1..MaxPrice : SupervisorStrike(s, p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

TapeHasNoRepeats ==
    \A i \in 1..Len(tape) : \A j \in 1..(i - 1) : tape[j] # tape[i]

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Symbols = {symACME, symZENO}
    Engines = {engPrimary, engBackup}
    MaxPrice = 2
    Span = 2
    NoEngine = noengine
    NoSymbol = nosymbol

INVARIANT TapeHasNoRepeats

\* Every auction struck is the end of the opening, not a deadlock.

nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction for each listed symbol. Striking a symbol's opening price is irreversible: the price goes onto the public tape, the auction for that symbol closes, and there is no mechanism to unstrike it or to amend the tape. A symbol must therefore appear on the tape at most once -- the tape is what the whole market prices off.

Two auction engines share the order book, and the right to strike is a lease on the book. The lease names one engine and carries a countdown of ticks; a tick of the exchange clock takes one off, and a lease with no ticks left has expired. An engine may take the lease when it is unheld or when the current lease has expired.

An engine holding a live lease, with nothing already prepared, may prepare a symbol whose auction is still open. Preparation is the engine's own working state and is not written to the book, so nothing about preparing a symbol stops another engine preparing the same symbol later.

Striking requires that the engine is still the lease holder, that its lease still has ticks left, and that the symbol it prepared is still open. Striking writes the price against the symbol, appends the symbol to the public tape, closes that symbol's auction and clears the engine's preparation. The "still open" test is doing real work: an engine can be left holding a preparation for a symbol that somebody else struck while its lease was expired.

An engine whose lease has gone, or has run out of ticks, may discard whatever it had prepared.

The market supervisor has a privileged override: any symbol whose auction is still open can be struck directly at a chosen price, with no lease at all, and the symbol is noted in the override register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No symbol ever appears more than once on the public tape.

    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoTech} \union Techs, ticks: 0..Span]

    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoTech, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ job = [t \in Techs |-> NoScript]

\* Nothing may be running on the arm when the lease changes hands.
Grant(t, s) ==

    /\ running = {} /\ job[t] = NoScript /\ s \notin filled
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> t, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ bus' = bus \union {t}
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![t] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, filled>>

    /\ running' = running \union {t}
    /\ bus' = bus \ {t}

    /\ filled' = filled \union {job[t]}
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![t] = NoScript]

    /\ lease' = [holder |-> NoTech, ticks |-> 0]

    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![t] = NoScript]

    NoScript = noscript

nl:
A pharmacy's dispensing cabinet has one robotic arm. The arm is the critical resource: exactly one technician's job may be running on it at a time, or the arm collides with itself and stock is spilled.

Access is regulated by a lease on the arm, naming one technician and carrying a countdown of ticks. A tick of the pharmacy clock takes one off; a lease with no ticks left has expired. A technician may be granted the lease when the lease is unheld or expired, when nothing at all is running on the arm, and when the technician has no job assigned; the grant names a prescription that has not yet been filled, assigns it to that technician, starts the countdown at its full span, and puts a grant acknowledgement onto the cabinet's internal bus.

The internal bus does not preserve order and acknowledgements are picked up independently, so an acknowledgement can arrive long after the grant it refers to has lapsed and been given to somebody else. A technician starts its job when it picks up an acknowledgement addressed to it, provided it is still the recorded lease holder and its lease still has ticks left. That holder test is the whole of the protection: without it a stale acknowledgement would put a second job on the arm.

A running job finishes regardless of the lease clock: the prescription is recorded as filled, the job is cleared, the technician comes off the arm, and the lease is released. A technician that is no longer the recorded holder may drop an acknowledgement addressed to it, and may abandon a job assigned to it if it is not running.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every technician with a job running on the arm is the technician currently recorded as holding the arm's lease, so two jobs never run at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription is eventually filled.

    /\ crashed = {}

Admit(c) ==
    /\ callState[c] = "new" /\ Cardinality(Queued) < QueueCap
    /\ ~FloorLive(FloorOf(c))
    /\ callState' = [callState EXCEPT ![c] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, committed, inHand, crashed>>

\* Backpressure: what will not fit is refused rather than queued.
Refuse(c) ==
    /\ callState[c] = "new"
    /\ \/ Cardinality(Queued) >= QueueCap
       \/ FloorLive(FloorOf(c))
    /\ callState' = [callState EXCEPT ![c] = "refused"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, committed, inHand, crashed>>

TakeCall(a, c) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ inHand[a] = NoCall /\ callState[c] = "queued"
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![a] = [call |-> c,
                                        snap |-> register[FloorOf(c)]]]
    /\ callState' = [callState EXCEPT ![c] = "taken"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, committed, crashed>>

\* The register is written back from the old reading; the durable count is
\* incremented in place.
Commit(a) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ inHand[a] # NoCall
    /\ inHand[a].snap < MaxServed
    /\ committed[FloorOf(inHand[a].call)] < MaxServed
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![FloorOf(inHand[a].call)] =
                        inHand[a].snap + 1]
    /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![FloorOf(inHand[a].call)] = @ + 1]
    /\ callState' = [callState EXCEPT ![inHand[a].call] = "done"]
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![a] = NoCall]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* Silent: the call stays in the crashed car's hands and nothing is said.
Crash(a) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, committed, callState, inHand>>

Reclaim(a) ==
    /\ a \in crashed /\ inHand[a] # NoCall
    /\ callState' = [callState EXCEPT ![inHand[a].call] = "queued"]
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![a] = NoCall]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, committed, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Calls : Admit(c) \/ Refuse(c)
    \/ \E a \in Cars, c \in Calls : TakeCall(a, c)
    \/ \E a \in Cars : Commit(a) \/ Crash(a) \/ Reclaim(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No lost updates: the register never falls behind the durable committed
\* count, so no service is written out of the register.
RegisterNeverLags ==
    \A f \in Floors : register[f] >= committed[f]
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Floors = {flLobby, flMezz}
    Tags = {tgUp, tgDown}
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    MaxServed = 2
    QueueCap = 1
    NoCall = nocall

INVARIANT RegisterNeverLags

\* Every call resolved with both cars idle is the end of the run, not a
\* deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An elevator bank keeps a shared hall-call register with one served-count per floor, and beside it a durable committed-count per floor that is incremented one at a time and never rewritten wholesale. The register must never fall behind the durable count: if it does, a service that really happened has been written out of the register and the floor will be dispatched to twice.

Hall calls are taken through a bounded dispatch queue that applies backpressure. A new call is admitted to the queue only if the queue is below its cap and no other call for the same floor is already queued or already taken by a car -- hall calls for a floor are coalesced, so at most one call per floor is ever live. A new call that cannot be admitted is refused outright and never runs.

A running car with nothing in hand may take a queued call. Taking it is also when the car reads the register: it writes down the served-count for that call's floor as it stands at that moment.

Committing writes the floor's served-count back as the figure the car wrote down plus one -- an absolute value derived from the old reading, not an increment of the current figure -- increments that floor's durable committed-count, marks the call done and empties the car's hands. The coalescing rule is what makes this safe: two cars must never be holding readings of the same floor at once.

Any car can crash silently. A crashed car stops doing anything at all: it keeps whatever call it was holding, and nothing is announced. The dispatcher can reclaim a call held by a crashed car, which puts the call back on the queue.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every floor, the hall-call register's served-count is never less than that floor's durable committed-count.

---- MODULE W4Od18m6p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Doors, Ids, Ctls, MaxIssued, Span, NoCtl, NoCode

Codes == Doors \X Ids

DoorOf(k) == k[1]

VARIABLES burnt, allowance, issued, lease, reserved

Vars == <<burnt, allowance, issued, lease, reserved>>

BurntFor(d) == {k \in burnt : DoorOf(k) = d}

Live(c) == lease.holder = c /\ lease.ticks > 0

NothingReserved == [c \in Ctls |-> NoCode]

TypeOK ==
    /\ burnt \subseteq Codes
    /\ allowance \in [Doors -> 0..MaxIssued]
    /\ issued \in [Doors -> 0..MaxIssued]
    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoCtl} \union Ctls, ticks: 0..Span]
    /\ reserved \in [Ctls -> {NoCode} \union [code: Codes,
                                             allowRead: 0..MaxIssued]]

Init ==
    /\ burnt = {}
    /\ allowance = [d \in Doors |-> MaxIssued]
    /\ issued = [d \in Doors |-> MaxIssued]
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoCtl, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ reserved = NothingReserved

\* Reissuing rebalances the door's allowance against what is already burnt,
\* and never leaves the door with no entry available.
Reissue(d, n) ==
    /\ lease.holder = NoCtl
    /\ n >= Cardinality(BurntFor(d)) + 1
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![d] = n]
    /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![d] = n - Cardinality(BurntFor(d))]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnt, lease, reserved>>

\* The hand-over voids every reservation: each one carries an allowance
\* reading that is no longer safe to act on.
TakeLease(c) ==
    /\ lease.holder = NoCtl \/ lease.ticks = 0
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> c, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ reserved' = NothingReserved
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnt, allowance, issued>>

Tick ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnt, allowance, issued, reserved>>

Reserve(c, k) ==
    /\ Live(c) /\ reserved[c] = NoCode
    /\ k \notin burnt /\ allowance[DoorOf(k)] > 0
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![c] =
                        [code |-> k, allowRead |-> allowance[DoorOf(k)]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnt, allowance, issued, lease>>

\* The irreversible step, writing the allowance back from the old reading.
Admit(c) ==
    /\ Live(c) /\ reserved[c] # NoCode
    /\ reserved[c].code \notin burnt /\ reserved[c].allowRead > 0
    /\ burnt' = burnt \union {reserved[c].code}
    /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![DoorOf(reserved[c].code)] =
                        reserved[c].allowRead - 1]
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![c] = NoCode]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, lease>>

Discard(c) ==
    /\ reserved[c] # NoCode /\ ~Live(c)
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![c] = NoCode]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnt, allowance, issued, lease>>

ReserveStep == \E c \in Ctls, k \in Codes : Reserve(c, k)

AdmitStep == \E c \in Ctls : Admit(c)

HomeStep ==
    \/ AdmitStep
    \/ \E c \in Ctls : TakeLease(c) \/ Discard(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctls, k \in Codes : Reserve(c, k)

Next == HomeStep \/ Tick \/ (\E d \in Doors, n \in 0..MaxIssued : Reissue(d, n))

\* Leases can be taken and left to lapse forever without anything being
\* reserved, so reserving and admitting both need strong fairness to get a
\* foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(HomeStep) /\ SF_Vars(ReserveStep) /\ SF_Vars(AdmitStep)

\* Irreversibility as a per-door accounting identity: entries available plus
\* codes burnt is always the entries issued, so no code is burnt twice.
DoorBooksBalance ==
    \A d \in Doors :
        allowance[d] + Cardinality(BurntFor(d)) = issued[d]

\* Progress: somebody really does get let in.
SomeGuestAdmitted == <>(burnt # {})
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Doors = {drFront, drSide}
    Ids = {gk1}
    Ctls = {ctlHub, ctlBridge}
    MaxIssued = 2
    Span = 2
    NoCtl = noctl
    NoCode = nocode

INVARIANT DoorBooksBalance
PROPERTY SomeGuestAdmitted

\* Every code burnt with no lease out is quiescent, not deadlocked.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network lets guests in on single-use codes. Spending a code is irreversible: the code is burnt on the way through the door and can never be reinstated, and the one-time entry it consumed out of that door's allowance can never be given back. Each door's books must always balance -- the entries still available on that door plus the codes already burnt for that door add up to exactly the number of entries currently issued for it.

The number of entries issued for a door is reconfigured while the network is running, as the household hands out and withdraws guest access. Reissuing a door sets a new issued figure and rebalances that door's remaining allowance against the codes already burnt for it; the new figure must leave the door at least one entry still available, and reissuing is only done while the lock controllers have no lease out.

Two lock controllers share the network, and the right to admit is a lease naming one controller with a countdown of ticks. A tick of the household clock takes one off; a lease with no ticks is expired. A controller may take the lease when it is unheld or expired. Taking it voids every reservation any controller was holding, because a reservation carries an allowance reading that the hand-over makes unsafe to act on.

A controller holding a live lease with nothing reserved may reserve a code that has not been burnt, provided its door still has an entry available; reserving records the code and the door's remaining-allowance figure as it read it.

Admitting is the irreversible step. It requires a live lease and that the reserved code has still not been burnt: the code goes on the burnt list and the door's remaining allowance is written back as the figure the controller read minus one -- an absolute value derived from that old reading. A controller whose lease has gone discards whatever it had reserved.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every door, the entries still available on that door plus the number of codes already burnt for that door always add up to exactly the number of entries currently issued for it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A guest is eventually let in -- some code is eventually burnt.
