---- MODULE W4Od5m5p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Proposals, Quorum, MaxRound, NoVote

VARIABLES round, lobby, counted, submitted, inFlight, applied

Vars == <<round, lobby, counted, submitted, inFlight, applied>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound /\ lobby \subseteq Players
    /\ counted \subseteq Players
    /\ submitted \in [Players -> 0..MaxRound]
    /\ inFlight \in [Players -> {NoVote} \union (0..MaxRound)]
    /\ applied \subseteq Proposals

Init ==
    /\ round = 0 /\ lobby = Players /\ counted = {}
    /\ submitted = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ inFlight = [p \in Players |-> NoVote]
    /\ applied = {}

\* Slow, not failed: the vote sits on the network carrying the round it was
\* cast in.
CastVote(p) ==
    /\ p \in lobby /\ inFlight[p] = NoVote /\ p \notin counted
    /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![p] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, lobby, counted, submitted, applied>>

LandVote(p) ==
    /\ inFlight[p] # NoVote /\ inFlight[p] = round /\ p \in lobby
    /\ counted' = counted \union {p}
    /\ submitted' = [submitted EXCEPT ![p] = inFlight[p]]
    /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![p] = NoVote]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, lobby, applied>>

DropVote(p) ==
    /\ inFlight[p] # NoVote
    /\ (inFlight[p] # round \/ p \notin lobby)
    /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![p] = NoVote]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, lobby, counted, submitted, applied>>

Carry(m) ==
    /\ Cardinality(counted) >= Quorum /\ m \notin applied
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ applied' = applied \union {m}
    /\ counted' = {} /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, submitted, inFlight>>

Join(p) ==
    /\ p \notin lobby /\ lobby' = lobby \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, counted, submitted, inFlight, applied>>

\* Emptying the tally is the point: once the roster changes, votes collected
\* under the old roster are not evidence about this lobby, and that goes for
\* players who are still happily present too.
Leave(p) ==
    /\ p \in lobby /\ Cardinality(lobby) - 1 >= Quorum
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ lobby' = lobby \ {p}
    /\ counted' = {} /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<submitted, inFlight, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : CastVote(p) \/ LandVote(p) \/ DropVote(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Join(p) \/ Leave(p)
    \/ \E m \in Proposals : Carry(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No unauthorised or stale vote counts: everyone in the tally is still in the
\* lobby and submitted in the round now open.
TallyIsCurrent ==
    \A p \in counted : p \in lobby /\ submitted[p] = round
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Players = {plAxe, plBolt, plCinder}
    Proposals = {mpDunes, mpVault}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxRound = 3
    NoVote = novote

INVARIANT TallyIsCurrent

\* With the round budget spent the lobby is settled, which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby changes map only by vote. A map change is carried when the live tally holds at least a quorum of votes from players currently in the lobby, and the lobby works in rounds: there is a round number, and only votes submitted in the round now open may sit in the tally.

Each player separately remembers the round it last submitted in, and nothing ever corrects that memory. Players are slow but they do not fail: a vote can be in flight across the network for a long time, and it carries the round it was cast in.

A player in the lobby with no vote already in flight and no vote already counted may cast one, which puts a vote in flight stamped with the round then open. A vote lands only if the round stamped on it is still the round open and the player who cast it is still in the lobby; landing records that player as counted and records the round it submitted in. A vote that fails either test is dropped off the network.

When the tally holds a quorum, any map change not already carried is carried: the change goes into the applied list, the tally is emptied and the round advances.

The roster changes under the vote. A player may join the lobby at any time, which disturbs nothing. A player may leave the lobby, as long as leaving keeps the lobby at least quorum-sized: leaving takes that player off the roster, empties the tally outright, and advances the round. Emptying the tally is the point -- once the roster has changed, the votes collected under the old roster are not evidence about the lobby that exists now, and that applies to the votes of players who are still perfectly happily present.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every player whose vote is in the live tally is still in the lobby and submitted that vote in the round now open.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Techs, Stock, HandCap, Quorum, MaxRound, NoTech, NoBallot

VARIABLES safe, held, given, round, motion, ballot

Vars == <<safe, held, given, round, motion, ballot>>

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

NoMotion == [tech |-> NoTech, qty |-> 0, safeRead |-> 0, rnd |-> 0]

Backing == Cardinality({v \in Techs : ballot[v] = round})

TypeOK ==
    /\ safe \in 0..(2 * Stock) /\ given \in 0..Stock
    /\ held \in [Techs -> 0..HandCap] /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ motion \in [tech: {NoTech} \union Techs, qty: 0..HandCap,
                   safeRead: 0..(2 * Stock), rnd: 0..MaxRound]
    /\ ballot \in [Techs -> {NoBallot} \union (0..MaxRound)]

Init ==
    /\ safe = Stock /\ given = 0
    /\ held = [t \in Techs |-> 0] /\ round = 0
    /\ motion = NoMotion
    /\ ballot = [t \in Techs |-> NoBallot]

OpenMotion(t, n) ==
    /\ motion.tech = NoTech /\ n <= safe /\ held[t] + n <= HandCap
    /\ motion' = [tech |-> t, qty |-> n, safeRead |-> safe, rnd |-> round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, held, given, round, ballot>>

CastBallot(v) ==
    /\ motion.tech # NoTech /\ ballot[v] # round
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![v] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, held, given, round, motion>>

\* The safe is written back from the mover's old count, so the round test is
\* what keeps that count true.  Executing closes the motion, so it has nothing
\* left to invalidate and does not advance the round.
Execute ==
    /\ motion.tech # NoTech /\ motion.rnd = round
    /\ Backing >= Quorum /\ motion.qty <= motion.safeRead
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![motion.tech] = @ + motion.qty]
    /\ safe' = motion.safeRead - motion.qty
    /\ motion' = NoMotion
    /\ UNCHANGED <<given, round, ballot>>

Abandon ==
    /\ motion.tech # NoTech /\ motion.rnd # round
    /\ motion' = NoMotion
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, held, given, round, ballot>>

\* Returning ampoules is a write to the safe, so it advances the round and
\* leaves any motion on the table recorded against a closed round.
Return(t, n) ==
    /\ held[t] >= n /\ n >= 1 /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = @ - n] /\ safe' = safe + n
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<given, motion, ballot>>

Administer(t) ==
    /\ held[t] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1] /\ given' = given + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<safe, round, motion, ballot>>

BallotStep == \E v \in Techs : CastBallot(v)

WardStep ==
    \/ BallotStep \/ Execute \/ Abandon
    \/ \E t \in Techs, n \in 1..HandCap : OpenMotion(t, n)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Administer(t)

Next == WardStep \/ (\E t \in Techs, n \in 1..HandCap : Return(t, n))

\* Returns advance the round and strand motions, so balloting and executing
\* need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(WardStep) /\ SF_Vars(BallotStep) /\ SF_Vars(Execute)

\* Conservation: safe plus hands plus administered is always exactly the
\* opening stock, so no execution mints or loses an ampoule.
AmpoulesConserved == safe + Tally(held, Techs) + given = Stock

\* Progress: an ampoule really does reach a patient.
SomethingAdministered == <>(given > 0)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Techs = {tcIvo, tcNell, tcOsei}
    Stock = 3
    HandCap = 2
    Quorum = 2
    MaxRound = 2
    NoTech = notech
    NoBallot = noballot

INVARIANT AmpoulesConserved
PROPERTY SomethingAdministered

\* An empty safe with everything administered is the end of the run, not a
\* deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital pharmacy accounts for every controlled ampoule it holds. An ampoule is in the safe, in a technician's hands, or already administered to a patient. The three together must always add up to exactly the stock the pharmacy opened with: ampoules are never conjured up and never lost.

Nothing leaves the safe on one person's authority. A withdrawal is put as a motion, and the motion needs a quorum of technician ballots. The pharmacy keeps a round number, and every write to the safe advances it, because a ballot cast about the safe as it was is not a ballot about the safe as it is.

Opening a motion, which is only possible when no motion is on the table, names the technician who will take the ampoules, how many, the round in force, and the number of ampoules the mover counted in the safe at that moment. Any technician may cast a ballot for the motion on the table; each technician has one ballot slot, stamped with the round it voted in.

Executing the motion requires that the round recorded on the motion is still the round in force and that the ballots stamped with that round reach quorum. Executing moves the ampoules into the named technician's hands and writes the safe count back as the figure the mover counted minus the quantity taken -- an absolute value derived from that old count, not a subtraction from the safe as it now stands. Executing does not advance the round, because it closes the motion as it goes and there is nothing left to invalidate.

Technicians are slow but they do not fail. A motion can sit on the table for a long time, and a technician may in the meantime return ampoules from its hands to the safe, which advances the round. That leaves the motion on the table recorded against a round that has closed; such a motion is abandoned.

A technician with ampoules in hand may administer one, which moves it into the administered tally.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The ampoules in the safe, plus the ampoules in the technicians' hands, plus the ampoules already administered always add up to exactly the stock the pharmacy opened with.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An ampoule is eventually administered.

---- MODULE W4Od12m7p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Docs, Units, MaxVer, NoDoc

VARIABLES reg, seen, copy, claimed, quarantined, crashed

Vars == <<reg, seen, copy, claimed, quarantined, crashed>>

Running(d) == d \notin crashed

\* `seen[d]` is the version d last read; nothing invalidates it, so a stale
\* haematologist keeps a copy of a releasable list that has moved on.
Current(d) == seen[d] = reg.ver

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [oncall: {NoDoc} \union Docs, ver: 0..MaxVer,
                releasable: SUBSET Units]
    /\ seen \in [Docs -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ copy \in [Docs -> SUBSET Units]
    /\ claimed \subseteq Units /\ quarantined \subseteq Units
    /\ crashed \subseteq Docs

Init ==
    /\ reg = [oncall |-> NoDoc, ver |-> 0, releasable |-> Units]
    /\ seen = [d \in Docs |-> MaxVer]
    /\ copy = [d \in Docs |-> {}]
    /\ claimed = {} /\ quarantined = {} /\ crashed = {}

\* Only the haematologist the register names is pushed its contents.
Refresh(d) ==
    /\ Running(d) /\ reg.oncall = d /\ ~Current(d)
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![d] = reg.ver]
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = reg.releasable]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claimed, quarantined, crashed>>

TakeOnCall(d) ==
    /\ Running(d) /\ reg.oncall = NoDoc /\ reg.ver < MaxVer
    /\ reg' = [oncall |-> d, ver |-> reg.ver + 1,
               releasable |-> reg.releasable]
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![d] = reg.ver + 1]
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = reg.releasable]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, quarantined, crashed>>

\* Claiming consults the haematologist's own copy, never the register, so the
\* version check is the only thing tying that copy to reality.
Claim(d, u) ==
    /\ Running(d) /\ Current(d)
    /\ u \in copy[d] /\ u \notin claimed
    /\ claimed' = claimed \union {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, seen, copy, quarantined, crashed>>

Pull(u) ==
    /\ u \in reg.releasable /\ u \notin claimed /\ reg.ver < MaxVer
    /\ reg' = [oncall |-> reg.oncall, ver |-> reg.ver + 1,
               releasable |-> reg.releasable \ {u}]
    /\ quarantined' = quarantined \union {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, copy, claimed, crashed>>

\* Silent: the register goes on naming the crashed haematologist as on call.
Crash(d) ==
    /\ Running(d) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, seen, copy, claimed, quarantined>>

ClearOnCall ==
    /\ reg.oncall \in crashed /\ reg.ver < MaxVer
    /\ reg' = [oncall |-> NoDoc, ver |-> reg.ver + 1,
               releasable |-> reg.releasable]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, copy, claimed, quarantined, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Docs : Refresh(d) \/ TakeOnCall(d) \/ Crash(d)
    \/ \E d \in Docs, u \in Units : Claim(d, u)
    \/ \E u \in Units : Pull(u)
    \/ ClearOnCall

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* No stale participant acts: a unit is never both claimed for release and
\* pulled into quarantine.
ClaimedAndQuarantinedDisjoint == claimed \cap quarantined = {}

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Docs = {dcFarr, dcOkoro}
    Units = {unPlasma, unPlatelet}
    MaxVer = 3
    NoDoc = nodoc

INVARIANT ClaimedAndQuarantinedDisjoint

\* A crashed-out bank with the register's version budget spent is stuck, which
\* is the outcome being modelled and not a deadlock to report.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood bank decides which units may be released, and which must be pulled, through a single shared register. The register holds three things: which haematologist is on call, a version number, and the releasable list -- the set of units currently cleared for release. Every write to the register advances the version number, and the register is only ever updated by compare-and-swap: a haematologist may write it only if the version it last read is still the version in the register.

A unit must never be both claimed for release and pulled into quarantine. Those two sets have to stay disjoint, because a unit that is claimed will go into a patient and a unit that is quarantined must not.

The register's contents are only pushed to the haematologist it names as on call. That haematologist, if it is running, may refresh: it takes a copy of the version number and a copy of the releasable list as they stand. When the register names nobody as on call, any running haematologist may take on call, which advances the version and gives that haematologist a fresh copy of the version and the releasable list.

A running haematologist may claim a unit for release if the version it last read is still the version in the register, the unit is on its own copy of the releasable list, and the unit is not already claimed. Note that claiming consults the haematologist's own copy of the list, never the register directly -- the version check is the only thing tying that copy to reality.

The laboratory pulls a unit into quarantine by removing it from the register's releasable list, which advances the version. It may only do this to a unit that is not already claimed.

Any haematologist can crash silently. A crashed one stops doing anything at all, and the register goes on naming it as on call with nothing announced. When the register names an on-call haematologist that has crashed, the laboratory clears the on-call field, which advances the version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No unit is ever both claimed for release and pulled into quarantine.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m0p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Blocks, Trains, Interlocks, MaxVer, NoReport

VARIABLES table, reported, ver, pending, logged

Vars == <<table, reported, ver, pending, logged>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ table \in [Blocks -> SUBSET Trains]
    /\ reported \in [Blocks -> SUBSET Trains]
    /\ ver \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ pending \in [Interlocks -> {NoReport} \union
                    [blk: Blocks, trn: Trains, snap: SUBSET Trains,
                     rv: 0..MaxVer]]
    /\ logged \subseteq Trains

Init ==
    /\ table = [b \in Blocks |-> {}] /\ reported = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]
    /\ ver = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ pending = [i \in Interlocks |-> NoReport]
    /\ logged = {}

\* Optimistic: the interlocking copies the whole entry and the version and
\* walks away with both.
Observe(i, b, t) ==
    /\ pending[i] = NoReport
    /\ t \notin reported[b] /\ t \notin logged
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = [blk |-> b, trn |-> t,
                                          snap |-> table[b], rv |-> ver[b]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<table, reported, ver, logged>>

\* The entry is written back wholesale from the copy, so the version test is
\* the only thing stopping a train added in between being written out again.
ApplyReport(i) ==
    /\ pending[i] # NoReport
    /\ pending[i].rv = ver[pending[i].blk]
    /\ ver[pending[i].blk] < MaxVer
    /\ table' = [table EXCEPT ![pending[i].blk] =
                    pending[i].snap \union {pending[i].trn}]
    /\ reported' = [reported EXCEPT ![pending[i].blk] =
                       @ \union {pending[i].trn}]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![pending[i].blk] = @ + 1]
    /\ logged' = logged \union {pending[i].trn}
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = NoReport]

DropReport(i) ==
    /\ pending[i] # NoReport
    /\ pending[i].rv # ver[pending[i].blk]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = NoReport]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<table, reported, ver, logged>>

LeaveBlock(b, t) ==
    /\ t \in table[b] /\ ver[b] < MaxVer
    /\ table' = [table EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {t}]
    /\ reported' = [reported EXCEPT ![b] = @ \ {t}]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, logged>>

ObserveStep == \E i \in Interlocks, b \in Blocks, t \in Trains : Observe(i, b, t)

ApplyStep == \E i \in Interlocks : ApplyReport(i)

DropStep == \E i \in Interlocks : DropReport(i)

SignalStep == ObserveStep \/ ApplyStep \/ DropStep

Next ==
    \/ ObserveStep
    \/ ApplyStep
    \/ DropStep
    \/ \E b \in Blocks, t \in Trains : LeaveBlock(b, t)

\* Trains coming and going churn the block versions, so observing and applying
\* need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(SignalStep) /\ SF_Vars(ObserveStep) /\ SF_Vars(ApplyStep)

\* No lost updates: block by block, the occupancy table is exactly the durable
\* reported set.
TableMatchesReported == \A b \in Blocks : table[b] = reported[b]

\* Progress: every train is logged.
AllTrainsLogged == <>(logged = Trains)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {bkNorthbound, bkSouthbound}
    Trains = {trA, trB}
    Interlocks = {ilCabin, ilRelay}
    MaxVer = 5
    NoReport = noreport

INVARIANT TableMatchesReported
PROPERTY AllTrainsLogged

\* With every block's version budget spent the interlockings are quiescent,
\* which is not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling system keeps a shared occupancy table: for each track block, the set of trains the signaller believes is standing in it. Beside the table there is a durable reported set per block, maintained one train at a time and never rewritten wholesale. The two must agree exactly, block by block -- if the table drops a train the reported set still has, a signal will be cleared into an occupied block.

There is no lock over the table. Each block carries a version number instead, and the interlockings work optimistically. An interlocking with nothing pending may observe a train that is not already reported in a block and has not yet been logged this run; observing copies the whole current contents of that block's table entry and the block's version number as they stand.

Reports travel over the trackside network, which does not preserve order, and each interlocking's report is picked up independently, so one can be applied long after it was made. Applying a report is only allowed if the block's version number is still the number recorded on the report. Applying writes the block's table entry back as the copy taken at observation time with the observed train added -- the whole entry, written wholesale from the copy -- adds that train to the block's durable reported set, advances the block's version, and logs the train.

An interlocking whose report no longer matches the block's version drops it and starts again.

A train standing in a block may leave it, which takes it out of both the table entry and the durable reported set for that block and advances the block's version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every block, the occupancy table's entry is exactly that block's durable reported set.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every train is eventually logged.

---- MODULE W4Od15m4p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Sizes, Ids, Engines, QueueCap, NoOrder

Orders == Sizes \X Ids

SizeOf(o) == o[1]

VARIABLES state, unmatched, matched, holding, tape

Vars == <<state, unmatched, matched, holding, tape>>

RECURSIVE Volume(_)
Volume(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN SizeOf(x) + Volume(S \ {x})

TotalVol == Volume(Orders)

Queued == {o \in Orders : state[o] = "queued"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ state \in [Orders -> {"new", "queued", "refused", "reserved",
                             "executed"}]
    /\ unmatched \in 0..(2 * TotalVol) /\ matched \in 0..TotalVol
    /\ holding \in [Engines -> {NoOrder} \union Orders]
    /\ tape \in Seq(Orders)

Init ==
    /\ state = [o \in Orders |-> "new"]
    /\ unmatched = TotalVol /\ matched = 0
    /\ holding = [e \in Engines |-> NoOrder]
    /\ tape = <<>>

Admit(o) ==
    /\ state[o] = "new" /\ Cardinality(Queued) < QueueCap
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![o] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unmatched, matched, holding, tape>>

\* Backpressure: what will not fit is refused rather than queued.
Refuse(o) ==
    /\ state[o] = "new" /\ Cardinality(Queued) >= QueueCap
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![o] = "refused"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unmatched, matched, holding, tape>>

Reserve(e, o) ==
    /\ holding[e] = NoOrder /\ state[o] = "queued"
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![e] = o]
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![o] = "reserved"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unmatched, matched, tape>>

\* Publishing does not release the reservation, so the "still only reserved"
\* test is what stops a slow engine moving the same volume twice.
Publish(e) ==
    /\ holding[e] # NoOrder /\ state[holding[e]] = "reserved"
    /\ SizeOf(holding[e]) <= unmatched
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![holding[e]] = "executed"]
    /\ unmatched' = unmatched - SizeOf(holding[e])
    /\ matched' = matched + SizeOf(holding[e])
    /\ tape' = Append(tape, holding[e])
    /\ UNCHANGED holding

Confirm(e) ==
    /\ holding[e] # NoOrder /\ state[holding[e]] = "executed"
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![e] = NoOrder]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, unmatched, matched, tape>>

Requeue(e) ==
    /\ holding[e] # NoOrder /\ state[holding[e]] = "reserved"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![holding[e]] = "queued"]
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![e] = NoOrder]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unmatched, matched, tape>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Admit(o) \/ Refuse(o)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, o \in Orders : Reserve(e, o)
    \/ \E e \in Engines : Publish(e) \/ Confirm(e) \/ Requeue(e)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Irreversibility as a volume identity: unmatched plus matched is always the
\* auction's opening volume, so no order's volume is matched twice.
AuctionBooksBalance == unmatched + matched = TotalVol
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Sizes = {1, 2}
    Ids = {lotA, lotB}
    Engines = {engMatch, engSpare}
    QueueCap = 2
    NoOrder = noorder

INVARIANT AuctionBooksBalance

\* Every order resolved with both engines idle is the end of the opening, not
\* a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange matches its opening auction through a bounded work queue. Publishing an execution report to the public tape is irreversible: the report is out, the volume is matched, and there is no mechanism to withdraw it. The auction's books must therefore always balance -- the volume still unmatched on the book plus the volume already matched onto the tape adds up to exactly the total volume the auction opened with, which is another way of saying no order is ever executed twice.

Orders arrive and are admitted to the work queue if the queue is below its cap. An order that will not fit is refused outright, with backpressure applied rather than the queue growing, and a refused order never runs.

Matching engines are slow but they do not fail. An engine with nothing reserved may reserve a queued order, which marks the order reserved. The engine then does the matching work, which takes as long as it takes.

Publishing requires that the order the engine holds is still merely reserved rather than already executed. Publishing marks the order executed, moves its volume off the unmatched side of the book and onto the matched side, and appends the order to the public tape. Publishing does not release the engine's reservation -- releasing is a separate confirmation step, allowed once the order the engine holds has been marked executed. That is exactly why publishing has to check the order is still only reserved: a slow engine that comes back round to publishing again must not move the same volume twice.

An engine may instead requeue an order it holds that is still only reserved, putting it back on the queue and releasing the reservation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The volume still unmatched on the book plus the volume already matched onto the tape always adds up to exactly the total volume the auction opened with, so no order's volume is ever matched twice.

---- MODULE W4Od16m6p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Scripts, Bins, Arms, Span, NoArm, NoBin, NoPlan

VARIABLES binOf, freeList, lease, plan, crashed, collected

Vars == <<binOf, freeList, lease, plan, crashed, collected>>

Running(a) == a \notin crashed

Live(a) == lease.holder = a /\ lease.ticks > 0

Allocated == {s \in Scripts : binOf[s] # NoBin}

NothingPending == [a \in Arms |-> NoPlan]

TypeOK ==
    /\ binOf \in [Scripts -> {NoBin} \union Bins]
    /\ freeList \subseteq Bins
    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoArm} \union Arms, ticks: 0..Span]
    /\ plan \in [Arms -> {NoPlan} \union [scr: Scripts, bin: Bins]]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Arms /\ collected \subseteq Scripts

Init ==
    /\ binOf = [s \in Scripts |-> NoBin] /\ freeList = Bins
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoArm, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ plan = NothingPending
    /\ crashed = {} /\ collected = {}

\* The hand-over voids every pending allocation: a bin chosen under the old
\* holder's view of the map is no longer safe to commit.
TakeLease(a) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ (lease.holder = NoArm \/ lease.ticks = 0)
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> a, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ plan' = NothingPending
    /\ UNCHANGED <<binOf, freeList, crashed, collected>>

Tick ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<binOf, freeList, plan, crashed, collected>>

PlanAllocation(a, s, b) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ Live(a) /\ plan[a] = NoPlan
    /\ binOf[s] = NoBin /\ b \in freeList
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![a] = [scr |-> s, bin |-> b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<binOf, freeList, lease, crashed, collected>>

\* Committing does not re-check the free list; the lease and the voiding of
\* pending allocations are what keep the planned bin free.
Commit(a) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ Live(a) /\ plan[a] # NoPlan
    /\ binOf[plan[a].scr] = NoBin
    /\ binOf' = [binOf EXCEPT ![plan[a].scr] = plan[a].bin]
    /\ freeList' = freeList \ {plan[a].bin}
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![a] = NoPlan]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, crashed, collected>>

Collect(s) ==
    /\ binOf[s] # NoBin /\ s \notin collected
    /\ freeList' = freeList \union {binOf[s]}
    /\ binOf' = [binOf EXCEPT ![s] = NoBin]
    /\ collected' = collected \union {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, plan, crashed>>

\* Silent: the lease and the pending allocation stay where they are.
Crash(a) ==
    /\ Running(a) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<binOf, freeList, lease, plan, collected>>

CollectStep == \E s \in Scripts : Collect(s)

Next ==
    \/ Tick \/ CollectStep
    \/ \E a \in Arms : TakeLease(a) \/ Commit(a) \/ Crash(a)
    \/ \E a \in Arms, s \in Scripts, b \in Bins : PlanAllocation(a, s, b)

\* Collection needs no arm, so it makes progress even after every arm has
\* crashed.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars /\ WF_Vars(CollectStep)

\* No double allocation: free bins plus allocated prescriptions always account
\* for every bin the cabinet has.
BinsFullyAccounted ==
    Cardinality(freeList) + Cardinality(Allocated) = Cardinality(Bins)

\* Progress: a prescription put in a bin does not sit there forever.
AllocatedGetsCollected ==
    \A s \in Scripts : (binOf[s] # NoBin) ~> (s \in collected)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Scripts = {rxTablet, rxSyrup}
    Bins = {bnOne, bnTwo}
    Arms = {armLeft, armRight}
    Span = 2
    NoArm = noarm
    NoBin = nobin
    NoPlan = noplan

INVARIANT BinsFullyAccounted
PROPERTY AllocatedGetsCollected

\* A fully crashed cabinet with everything collected is stuck, which is the
\* outcome being modelled and not a deadlock to report.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A pharmacy dispenser holds made-up prescriptions in numbered collection bins. A bin takes exactly one prescription, so a bin must never be allocated to two prescriptions at once -- the second patient would open the bin and find somebody else's medicine. The cabinet keeps a free-bin list alongside the allocation map, and the books have to balance: the number of bins on the free list plus the number of prescriptions holding a bin always equals the number of bins the cabinet has.

The robot arms that load the bins work under a lease on the allocation map. The lease names one arm and carries a countdown of ticks; a tick of the cabinet clock takes one off, and a lease with no ticks left has expired. A running arm may take the lease when it is unheld or expired. Taking the lease voids every pending allocation any arm was holding, because a pending allocation names a bin that the arm chose while it held the map and that choice is no longer safe once the map has changed hands.

A running arm holding a live lease, with nothing pending, may plan an allocation: it names a prescription that does not yet hold a bin and a bin currently on the free list. Planning writes nothing to the map.

Committing requires a live lease and that the prescription still holds no bin: the prescription is recorded against the planned bin and that bin is struck off the free list. Note that committing does not re-check the free list -- the lease, and the voiding of pending allocations when it changes hands, are what make the planned bin still free.

A patient may collect any prescription that has been allocated a bin and not yet collected, which marks it collected, clears the allocation and puts the bin back on the free list.

Any arm can crash silently: it stops doing anything at all, keeping the lease if it held one and keeping whatever it had pending, with nothing announced.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of bins on the free list plus the number of prescriptions currently holding a bin always equals the number of bins the cabinet has, so no bin is ever allocated to two prescriptions.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription that has been allocated a bin is eventually collected.

---- MODULE W4Od11m1p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, Jobs, MaxGen

Presses == 0..(RingSize - 1)

Onward(p) == (p + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES ringGen, tok, driving, crashed, finished

Vars == <<ringGen, tok, driving, crashed, finished>>

Running(p) == p \notin crashed

\* Stuck when no running press holds the current generation's token.
Stuck == \A p \in Presses : (tok[p] = ringGen) => p \in crashed

TypeOK ==
    /\ ringGen \in 0..MaxGen /\ tok \in [Presses -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ driving \subseteq Presses /\ crashed \subseteq Presses
    /\ finished \subseteq Jobs

\* Generation one, so a press holding nothing cannot be mistaken for a press
\* holding the current token.
Init ==
    /\ ringGen = 1
    /\ tok = [p \in Presses |-> IF p = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ driving = {} /\ crashed = {} /\ finished = {}

PassToken(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ tok[p] = ringGen /\ p \notin driving
    /\ ringGen < MaxGen
    /\ ringGen' = ringGen + 1
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![p] = 0, ![Onward(p)] = ringGen + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<driving, crashed, finished>>

BeginDriving(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ tok[p] = ringGen /\ p \notin driving
    /\ driving' = driving \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ringGen, tok, crashed, finished>>

FinishJob(p, j) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ p \in driving /\ j \notin finished
    /\ driving' = driving \ {p}
    /\ finished' = finished \union {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ringGen, tok, crashed>>

\* Silent: the token stays held and the press stays clamped on the line.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ Running(p) /\ crashed' = crashed \union {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ringGen, tok, driving, finished>>

\* The hard reset releases any crashed press clamped on the line, which is
\* what stops it double-driving with the fresh token holder.
Repair(q) ==
    /\ Stuck /\ Running(q) /\ ringGen < MaxGen
    /\ ringGen' = ringGen + 1
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![q] = ringGen + 1]
    /\ driving' = driving \ crashed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, finished>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Presses : PassToken(p) \/ BeginDriving(p) \/ Crash(p)
                          \/ Repair(p)
    \/ \E p \in Presses, j \in Jobs : FinishJob(p, j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Mutual exclusion of the finishing line, stated as the literal property.
AtMostOneDrives ==
    \A p, q \in Presses : (p \in driving /\ q \in driving) => p = q

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Jobs = {jbFlyer, jbBook}
    MaxGen = 4

INVARIANT AtMostOneDrives

\* A crashed-out shop with the generation budget spent is stuck, which is the
\* outcome being modelled and not a deadlock to report.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A print shop runs several presses that share one finishing line -- the stapler and binder unit at the end of the floor. The finishing line is the critical resource: exactly one press may be driving it at a time, or sheets from two jobs get bound into the same book.

The right to drive the finishing line circulates as a ring token. The ring register holds a generation number, and each press separately holds the generation of the token it has, or nothing at all. Exactly one token is ever minted per generation. The shop opens on generation one with the first press holding the token and no other press holding anything.

A press that is running, holds the current generation's token and is not driving the finishing line may pass the token to the next press around the ring: the generation advances, the receiving press is given the new generation, and the passing press is left holding nothing. A press that is running and holds the current generation's token may begin driving the finishing line. A press that is running and driving may finish a job, which takes it off the line and records the job as finished.

Any press can crash silently. A crashed press stops doing anything at all: it keeps whatever token it held, it stays clamped on the finishing line if it was driving, and nothing is announced.

The ring is stuck when no running press holds the current generation's token. In that case the ring can be repaired: the generation advances, a running press of the shop's choosing is given the new token, and the finishing-line interlock is hard-reset, which mechanically releases any crashed press that was clamped on the line. Releasing them is essential -- a crashed press still clamped on the line while a fresh token holder starts driving is exactly the double-drive the shop is trying to avoid.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one press is ever driving the finishing line.

---- MODULE W4Od15m6p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Engines, Symbols, Span, MaxImb, NoEngine

VARIABLES lease, running, imbalance, published, seizures

Vars == <<lease, running, imbalance, published, seizures>>

Idle == [holder |-> NoEngine, ticks |-> 0]

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [holder: {NoEngine} \union Engines, ticks: 0..Span]
    /\ running \subseteq Engines
    /\ imbalance \in [Symbols -> 0..MaxImb]
    /\ published \subseteq Symbols /\ seizures \subseteq Engines

Init ==
    /\ lease = Idle /\ running = {}
    /\ imbalance = [s \in Symbols |-> 0]
    /\ published = {} /\ seizures = {}

\* Nothing may be running when the lease moves, which is what stops it going
\* out from under a run in progress.
GrantLease(e) ==
    /\ (lease.holder = NoEngine \/ lease.ticks = 0) /\ running = {}
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> e, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, imbalance, published, seizures>>

Tick ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, imbalance, published, seizures>>

\* Starting needs ticks left; a run already under way is not cut short by the
\* clock running down.
StartRun(e) ==
    /\ lease.holder = e /\ lease.ticks > 0 /\ e \notin running
    /\ running' = running \union {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, imbalance, published, seizures>>

Compute(e, s, v) ==
    /\ e \in running
    /\ imbalance' = [imbalance EXCEPT ![s] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, running, published, seizures>>

Publish(e, s) ==
    /\ e \in running /\ s \notin published
    /\ published' = published \union {s}
    /\ running' = running \ {e} /\ lease' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<imbalance, seizures>>

StopRun(e) ==
    /\ e \in running
    /\ running' = running \ {e} /\ lease' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<imbalance, published, seizures>>

\* The privileged path clears the calculator: otherwise the cut-off engine
\* would still be running when the installed engine starts.
Seize(e) ==
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> e, ticks |-> Span]
    /\ running' = {}
    /\ seizures' = seizures \union {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<imbalance, published>>

StartStep == \E e \in Engines : StartRun(e)

PublishStep == \E e \in Engines, s \in Symbols : Publish(e, s)

FloorStep ==
    \/ StartStep \/ PublishStep
    \/ \E e \in Engines : GrantLease(e) \/ StopRun(e)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, s \in Symbols, v \in 0..MaxImb : Compute(e, s, v)

Next == FloorStep \/ Tick \/ (\E e \in Engines : Seize(e))

\* Leases lapse before a run starts and the supervisor cuts runs off, so
\* starting and publishing need strong fairness to get a foot in that churn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
    /\ WF_Vars(FloorStep) /\ SF_Vars(StartStep) /\ SF_Vars(PublishStep)

\* Mutual exclusion of the calculator: whoever is running is the recorded
\* lease holder, and the record names at most one engine.
OnlyLeaseHolderRuns == \A e \in running : lease.holder = e

\* Progress: every symbol's opening reaches the tape.
AllSymbolsPublished == <>(published = Symbols)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Engines = {engAlpha, engDelta}
    Symbols = {symNOVA, symORCA}
    Span = 2
    MaxImb = 2
    NoEngine = noengine

INVARIANT OnlyLeaseHolderRuns
PROPERTY AllSymbolsPublished

\* Every symbol published with the calculator idle is the end of the opening,
\* not a deadlock.
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange computes its opening auction on a single imbalance calculator. The calculator is the critical resource: exactly one auction engine may be running on it at a time, or two engines overwrite each other's working figures and the published opening is nonsense.

Access is a lease on the calculator, naming one engine and carrying a countdown of ticks. A tick of the exchange clock takes one off, and a lease with no ticks left has expired. An engine may be granted the lease when the lease is unheld or expired -- and only when nothing at all is running on the calculator, which is what stops the lease moving out from under a run in progress.

An engine that is the recorded lease holder, with ticks still left on its lease, and not already running, may start a run. A running engine may write an imbalance figure for any symbol into the calculator's shared output. A running engine may publish a symbol that has not yet been published, which records the symbol as published, ends the run and releases the lease. A running engine may also just stop, which ends the run and releases the lease without publishing anything.

Note that starting a run needs ticks left on the lease, but a run already under way is not cut short by the lease clock running down; the run ends when the engine publishes or stops.

The market supervisor has a privileged override: the lease can be handed to any engine on the spot, whatever the clock says and whatever is running. Doing so clears the calculator -- whatever run was under way is cut off -- and the engine is noted in the seizure register. Clearing the calculator is essential, because otherwise the cut-off engine would still be running while the engine the supervisor just installed starts its own run.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every engine running on the imbalance calculator is the engine currently recorded as holding the calculator's lease, so two engines never run at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every symbol's opening is eventually published.
